d: Install Materix UI with npm, a CDN or plain files, import only the components you use, use the TypeScript types, load Roboto and Material Icons, and start from a minimal HTML template.

s.x: Materix UI ships as a full bundle (one CSS and one JS file) and as per-component ES modules for bundlers. It has no runtime dependencies. Choose npm (with a bundler), a CDN or plain files ( <link> + <script>).

npm run build generates dist/: File Format Use it when dist/materix.min.css Single CSS file with tokens, base styles, every component and the utilities You use the full bundle. dist/materix.es.js ES module ( import) with every component You work with Vite, webpack, Rollup or <script type="module">. dist/materix.umd.js UMD: exposes the window.Materix global You load the library with a classic <script>. dist/materix.umd.cjs Same UMD as CommonJS require('@rubenchodev/materix-ui') (Node, Jest). dist/components/{name}.js One component (ES module); it imports the CSS it needs You import only what you use. dist/components/{name}.css /.bundle.css The component’s own styles / with its dependencies Styles without the JS module. dist/core.js Registry, lifecycle, ComponentBase, emit, theme, i18n, positioning Per-component usage. dist/base.css / dist/utilities.css Tokens + base styles / utility classes Per-component usage. dist/chunks/* Shared code of the per-component modules Never imported directly. The package also ships the TypeScript declarations in types/.

Import the JS and the CSS in your application’s entry point: @rubenchodev/materix-ui resolves to dist/materix.es.js (with import) or to dist/materix.umd.cjs (with require). @rubenchodev/materix-ui/dist/materix.min.css keeps working as well. You can also import by name: Importing already initializes Importing the library registers every component and initializes the [data-mtx] elements present in the document. You don’t need to call initAll() except for content you add later. See Initialization.

With a bundler you can ship only the components you use. Each @rubenchodev/materix-ui/components/{name} module registers its component, schedules an automatic initAll() (when the DOM is ready) and imports its own CSS plus the CSS of the components it uses inside. Importing the module is enough; you only add base.css (tokens and base styles) once. {name} is the component folder: button, text-field, date-time-picker, toggle-button, app-bar … The shared JavaScript core and every CSS file are bundled once, even if several components import them (the bundler deduplicates each components/{name}.css module). For reference, a Vite app that uses only Button weighs about 28 kB of JS (9 kB gzip) and 30 kB of CSS (5 kB gzip); one that uses only Autocomplete, 81 kB of JS (22 kB gzip) and 72 kB of CSS (10 kB gzip). The full bundle is 414 kB / 373 kB. The modules import.css files, so they need a bundler that handles CSS imports (Vite, webpack with css-loader, Parcel, Rollup with a CSS plugin…). Without a bundler, use the full bundle. Available stylesheets per component: File Contents Use it when @rubenchodev/materix-ui/components/{name}.css Only that component’s styles (no dependencies). Fine con

The declarations ship with the package (no @types package needed): every component class with its public methods, the core API with generics and the mtx:* events typed as CustomEvent. Per-component modules have their own types ( @rubenchodev/materix-ui/components/button, @rubenchodev/materix-ui/core). For the UMD global in plain scripts, add /// <reference types="@rubenchodev/materix-ui" />.

Any CDN that serves npm packages works with the same paths. Always pin the exact version: With unpkg: https://unpkg.com/@rubenchodev/materix-ui@0.3.1/dist/materix.umd.js. The per-component JavaScript modules import CSS files, which browsers cannot load as modules: from a CDN, use the full bundle (the components/{name}.bundle.css files can be linked if you only need styles).

Copy dist/materix.min.css and dist/materix.umd.js into your project and link them: The script exposes the Materix global with the entire public API: Script loading order Place materix.umd.js at the end of the <body> (or in the <head> with defer). Your own scripts that use Materix must come after it and, if they run in the <head>, wrap their logic in document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',...). A script that calls Materix.getInstance() before the library loads gets Materix is not defined, and one that runs before the DOM is ready gets undefined as the instance.

The typeface ( --mtx-font-family) is Roboto and icons use the Material Icons font (.material-icons class). The library does not bundle them: load them yourself in the <head>. Weights 300, 400, 500 and 700 cover the whole type scale ( h1 / h2 headings use 300, buttons and subtitle2 use 500, <strong> uses 700). Without Roboto, components still work with the Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif fallback. Without Material Icons, attributes such as data-start-icon="email" display the icon name as text.

Copy it, save it as index.html and open it in your browser: The mtx-root class on <body> applies the library’s base styles: box-sizing: border-box, font, text color, the theme’s background color, color-scheme and the visible focus ring. Without it, components still render, but the rest of the page does not inherit the theme. <html lang="en"> also determines the language of the components’ built-in strings (calendar, Select search box, pagination). See Internationalization.
Read Quick start to understand the single-element syntax and the naming conventions.

d: The Materix UI mental model: write one element with data-mtx and the library builds the structure, the state and the accessibility.

s.x: You write a single HTML element with data-mtx plus data-* attributes. When the page loads, Materix builds the internal structure (label, outline, icons, helper text), wires up the events and applies the ARIA attributes. No JavaScript required.

Colombia Mexico Spain Create account The controls are still native <input>, <select> and <button> elements: they are submitted with the form, honor name, required, disabled and value, and work with the browser’s built-in validation.

A single semantic element. Configuration goes in data-* attributes: What happens on initialization: Materix wraps the <input> in a.mtx-text-field container and moves the data-* attributes and classes onto it. It generates the floating <label>, the notched outline ( outlined), the icons and the helper text. It preserves the <input> ’s original attributes ( id, name, value, required, disabled …) and assigns it an id if it has none, to link the label. It marks the element with data-mtx-initialized and stores the instance in the registry. This process is called auto-scaffolding and it is idempotent: initializing twice does not duplicate anything.

If you render on the server and want to control every node, write the full structure. Materix detects that it already exists and simply binds to it: Both syntaxes produce the same visual result. Each component page documents its BEM structure in the Full BEM syntax section. Buttons: classes, not data-variant Button, IconButton and Fab are built on the native <button> and their variant is declared with classes: class="mtx-button mtx-button--contained". data-mtx="button" adds the ripple, the size ( data-size) and the disabled state on links. See the modifiers on the Button page.

Convention Form Example Prefix Everything in the library starts with mtx- mtx-card, --mtx-color-primary BEM block mtx-{component} mtx-text-field BEM element mtx-{component}__{element} mtx-text-field__label BEM modifier mtx-{component}--{modifier} mtx-button--outlined, mtx-button--small Initialization data-mtx="{component}" in kebab-case data-mtx="date-picker" Options data-{option} in kebab-case data-start-icon, data-helper-text Internal state data-mtx-initialized (set by the library; don’t write it) — Tokens --mtx-* CSS variables --mtx-shape-radius Events mtx:{component}:{action} mtx:dialog:close Theme data-mtx-theme on <html> data-mtx-theme="dark" Global API Materix object (UMD) or named imports (ESM) Materix.getInstance(el)

The declarative syntax covers the common cases. When you need to control a component from code, retrieve the instance that auto-initialization already created: For an element without data-mtx (for example, one created from JavaScript), instantiate the class directly: Don’t use new Materix.X(el) on an element that already has data-mtx: auto-initialization has already created an instance and you would end up with two, with duplicated events. Use Materix.getInstance(el) or Materix.init(el), which returns the existing one. Each component’s methods are listed in its API reference section. The full lifecycle (when initialization happens, dynamic content, events) is covered in Initialization.

d: How and when Materix UI creates and destroys instances: auto-initialization, initAll, init, getInstance, watch, lifecycle (destroy, destroyAll), custom components and mtx:* events.

s.x: Materix automatically initializes every [data-mtx] element on the page. You only need JavaScript for content added later, to get an instance or to listen for events.

Function Returns Usage initAll(root = document) void Initializes every pending [data-mtx] inside root (including root itself). init(element, name?) instance or null Initializes a single element. name forces the component and writes data-mtx if missing. initElement(element, name?) instance or null Same as init ( init is its alias). getInstance(element) instance or undefined Returns the instance already created for that element. watch(root = document, { destroyOnRemove }) MutationObserver Automatically initializes whatever is added to root (and destroys what is removed with destroyOnRemove: true). destroy(element) boolean Destroys the instance of an element: listeners, timers, registry. destroyAll(root = document) number Destroys every instance inside root. registerComponent(name, Class) void Registers a class for data-mtx="name". All of them are available on the Materix global (UMD) and as named exports (ESM).

When it loads, the library runs initAll(): if the document is still loading, it waits for DOMContentLoaded; if the DOM is already ready (for example, a <script type="module"> or a script at the end of the <body>), it initializes immediately. For each element with data-mtx, it looks up the class registered under that name, creates the instance, stores it in the registry and marks the element with data-mtx-initialized. data-mtx values that are not registered are silently ignored.

Initializing twice does not create two instances: initAll repeats the pass over the container (up to five times) only while the previous pass created new instances. This way it also initializes [data-mtx] components that another component generates during its own auto-scaffolding, without rescanning in vain when there are data-mtx values that are not registered.

new Materix.Button(el) on an element that already has an instance of the same component (the same class, or a subclass in either direction, such as new MyButton(el) over a Button) destroys the previous instance first (listeners, timers, registry) and registers the new one, so listeners are never duplicated. Prefer Materix.init(el) or getInstance(el) when you just want the current instance: they reuse it instead of recreating it. Instances of an unrelated class on the same node are kept (for example, a declarative Tooltip on an IconButton).

If the element was already initialized, it returns the existing instance. It returns null if there is no component name, if the name is not registered or if element is not an element ( init(null) is a safe no-op).

With the simplified syntax, the component may wrap your element in a generated container (TextField, Checkbox, Switch…). The registry stores the instance under both elements, so getInstance works with your original <input> as well as with the.mtx-* container. instance.element is always the component’s root element. getInstance returns undefined if it is called before auto-initialization. Run your code after the library has loaded, and inside DOMContentLoaded if your script lives in the <head>.

When you insert HTML after the page has loaded, initialize it by passing the container: initAll(container) only walks that subtree and skips whatever was already initialized, so it is safe to call it every time the content changes.

watch(root) creates a MutationObserver on root ( childList and subtree). For every added node, it initializes the node itself if it has data-mtx, plus all of its [data-mtx] descendants. It returns the observer so you can stop it: watch is not active by default. It only reacts to added nodes (see Lifecycle for destroyOnRemove): changing the data-mtx attribute of an existing element does not initialize it. Observe the smallest container possible; observing document on a page with many mutations has a cost.

s.h: Destroying instances: destroy, destroyAll and instance.destroy()
s.x: Every component extends ComponentBase, so every instance has destroy(). It frees resources and unlinks the instance: removes the listeners it registered on document, window and on external elements (triggers, scroll containers…); cancels its timers, animation frames and observers ( ResizeObserver, MutationObserver, matchMedia); closes it first if it is open (Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Select, Snackbar) and removes the nodes it moved to <body> (Menu popper, Drawer backdrop) or brings them back (Select menu); removes it from the registry and removes data-mtx-initialized from its elements (the original one and the generated root): afterwards getInstance(el) returns undefined and initAll() can initialize it again. Function Returns Usage destroy(element) boolean Destroys the instance linked to element (original or generated root). false if there was none. If the component’s destroy() throws, the instance is unlinked anyway and the error is rethrown; destroyAll() logs it and continues with the rest. destroyAll(root = document) number Destroys every initialized component inside root (including root), deepest first. instance.destroy() void Same as destroy(element). Idempotent: calling it twice

With destroyOnRemove, the observer also destroys the instances of the nodes removed from root. A node that is only moved (removed and inserted again in the same batch of mutations, as the auto-scaffolding does) is not destroyed. Components whose surface is moved to <body> (Menu’s popper, an open Popover) leave a marker comment in their original place: when that place is removed, destroyOnRemove (and destroyAll(view)) destroys them as well, so nothing is left orphaned in <body>. Tooltips close by themselves when their trigger leaves the DOM.

s.h: Your own components: this.listen() and this.onDestroy()
s.x: Inside a ComponentBase subclass, register listeners with this.listen(target, type, handler, options) and any other cleanup with this.onDestroy(fn): destroy() runs them all. If you override destroy(), call super.destroy(). Method Returns Usage listen(target, type, handler, options?) Function Adds a listener that destroy() removes. Returns a function to remove it earlier. onDestroy(fn) void Registers a cleanup (observer, timer, portaled node…) for destroy(). destroy() void Runs the cleanups, unlinks the instance and sets instance.destroyed = true.

Extend ComponentBase and register the class under the name you will use in data-mtx: ComponentBase provides element, listen(), onDestroy(), destroy(), the disabled getter and the disable() and enable() methods (backed by the native disabled property). Register first, or call initAll again Auto-initialization runs when the library loads. If you register your component afterwards, its elements stay uninitialized until you call initAll(). Registering an existing name silently replaces the previous class: use your own name that doesn’t collide with Materix’s.
Components dispatch CustomEvent s with bubbles: true, so you can listen on the element itself or delegate to an ancestor. The data lives in event.detail.

Every event is named mtx:{component}:{action}: {component} is the data-mtx name in kebab-case and {action} a verb or a kebab-case noun ( open, close, change, page-change …). Global events use the module name ( mtx:locale:change, mtx:theme:change). Event Component detail Fired when mtx:accordion:change Accordion { expanded } The panel expands or collapses. mtx:alert:open / mtx:alert:close Alert — The alert is shown / closed. mtx:breadcrumbs:expand Breadcrumbs — The collapsed items are expanded. mtx:breadcrumbs:navigate Breadcrumbs { index, href, label, … } An item is activated. Cancelable. mtx:chip:click / mtx:chip:delete Chip {} A clickable chip is activated / the delete action runs. mtx:dialog:open / mtx:dialog:close Dialog — / { reason } The dialog opens / closes. mtx:drawer:open / mtx:drawer:close Drawer — / { reason } The drawer opens / closes. mtx:drawer:mode-change Drawer { mode, previousMode } A responsive drawer crosses its breakpoint. mtx:list:select ListItemButton { item } A list item is selected. mtx:menu:open / mtx:menu:close Menu — The menu opens / closes. mtx:menu:select Menu { item, checked? } An item is chosen. mtx:pagination:change Pagination { page, previousPage,

Events renamed to the convention keep dispatching their old name, with the same detail, right after the new one. The aliases will be removed in 1.0: migrate your listeners. Old name (deprecated) New name mtx-select mtx:list:select mtx:change (RadioGroup) mtx:radio-group:change mtx:password-visibility mtx:text-field:password-visibility mtx:adornment-click mtx:text-field:adornment-click mtx:drawer:modechange mtx:drawer:mode-change mtx-speed-dial-open / mtx-speed-dial-close mtx:speed-dial:open / mtx:speed-dial:close mtx:localechange mtx:locale:change mtx:theme-change mtx:theme:change Don't listen to both names Both the new event and its alias are dispatched for the same action. Listening to both would run your handler twice. Your own components can follow the same pattern with the emit(target, name, detail, { aliases, cancelable }) helper of src/core/events.js (it returns false if the event or an alias was canceled). Form controls (TextField, Select, NativeSelect, Checkbox, Radio, Switch) also fire the native input and change events on the <input> or <select>. Select and DateTimePicker fire a native change when the value changes through their UI.

d: Mobile-first mtx-* classes for display, flex, alignment, gap, spacing, sizing, text, color, position, borders and elevation, to build layouts without custom CSS.

s.x: Materix ships a system of single-purpose utility classes, Bootstrap-style, with MUI’s tokens and look. Together with Container, Stack and Grid they let you lay out a whole application without writing custom CSS: your stylesheet is left only for branding (illustrations, gradients, charts). They all start with mtx- and use!important, so they always win over component styles. Values come from the --mtx-* tokens: they follow the light/dark theme and your brand theme. They ship in materix.min.css; no JavaScript required.

Responsive utilities are mobile-first: the class without an infix applies from 0px and the class with an infix applies from that width up ( min-width). The infix goes right after the group: mtx-d-md-none, mtx-p-lg-4, mtx-flex-sm-row, mtx-text-md-start. Infix Min width Example (none) 0px mtx-d-none sm 600px mtx-d-sm-block md 900px mtx-flex-md-row lg 1200px mtx-gap-lg-4 xl 1536px mtx-px-xl-6 xs sm md lg xl
Gap, margin and padding use the {n} scale = 0, 0_5, 1, 1_5, 2, 2_5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, i.e. n × 8px through the --mtx-spacing-{n} tokens ( 0_5 = 4px, 1_5 = 12px, 2_5 = 20px).

d: Enable the dark theme, switch it with Materix.theme, follow the system preference, build a brand theme by overriding tokens, and browse every --mtx-* variable.

s.x: Every aspect of Materix’s look comes from --mtx-* CSS variables (design tokens). Components never use hard-coded colors: changing a token changes every component that consumes it. A theme is simply a set of values for those tokens.

The light theme is the default. For the dark theme, add data-mtx-theme="dark" to <html>: To make the page background and text follow the theme, put class="mtx-root" on <body>: it applies --mtx-color-background-default, --mtx-color-text-primary and the matching color-scheme (dark scrollbars and native controls).

The library includes a small API to read and change the theme, available as Materix.theme (UMD) or import { theme } from '@rubenchodev/materix-ui' (ES modules). It writes the effective theme to <html data-mtx-theme> and the chosen mode to <html data-mtx-theme-mode>. On load it only reads the current attribute: if your page sets nothing, nothing changes. Method Returns Description theme.get() 'light' | 'dark' Effective theme (with system, the one the OS prefers). theme.getMode() 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' Chosen mode. theme.set(mode, { persist? }) 'light' | 'dark' Applies light, dark or system. Saves it if persistence is on ( persist: false skips saving once). Throws TypeError for other values. theme.toggle() 'light' | 'dark' Switches between light and dark (from system, to the opposite of the effective theme). theme.configure({ persist, query }) 'light' | 'dark' Turns on persistence ( true or a localStorage key) and the URL parameter ( true or a parameter name) and applies the saved/forced mode. theme.sync(root?) void Re-syncs toggle buttons inserted after load. mtx:theme:change (deprecated alias until 1.0: mtx:theme-change) is dispatched on document whenever the effective theme o

Any element with data-mtx-theme-toggle works without JavaScript: No value: switches between light and dark. It gets aria-pressed ( true in dark), a stable aria-label from the i18n dictionary ( Dark theme / Tema oscuro), a title with the next action ( Switch to light theme …) and its.material-icons changes between dark_mode and light_mode (customizable with data-icon-light / data-icon-dark; data-mtx-theme-static-icon leaves it untouched). With a value ( light, dark or system): sets that mode and marks aria-pressed="true" on the active button, which suits a segmented control. An aria-label, aria-labelledby or visible text written by you is never overwritten. Light Dark System

Both are opt-in and are declared on <html>: Attribute on <html> Value Effect data-mtx-theme light | dark | system Initial mode ( light if absent). data-mtx-theme-persist empty or storage key Saves every set() /toggle and restores it on load. data-mtx-theme-query empty or parameter name?theme= forces the mode on load without saving it (handy for screenshots and links). Priority on load: URL parameter, saved value, data-mtx-theme-mode / data-mtx-theme, light. The same options exist in JavaScript: Materix.theme.configure({ persist: 'my-key', query: true }).

The library is usually loaded at the end of <body>, so a saved dark theme would be applied after the first paint. Render data-mtx-theme on the server, or add this inline snippet in the <head>, before the CSS; the library then picks up the same value: Any value of data-mtx-theme other than dark keeps the light tokens: the CSS only reads [data-mtx-theme='dark'].

Override the tokens in your own stylesheet, loaded after materix.min.css. Always declare both blocks, light and dark: Override every token in both blocks:root and [data-mtx-theme='dark'] have the same specificity. When <html> carries the dark theme, both selectors match and the last one declared wins. Since your:root loads after Materix’s CSS, a token you redefine only in:root will also override the library’s dark value. If you change a color in:root, give it its dark value in your [data-mtx-theme='dark'] block as well. Guidelines for choosing values: -contrast is the color of text on top of the main color: it must have a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 (WCAG AA). -dark is used for the hover state of contained buttons and FABs; -light for subtle backgrounds (the calendar range) and for the Snackbar action. -text ( --mtx-color-{color}-text) is the color for text and icons of that color on the background (text/outlined Button, Link, Typography…). By default it reaches 4.5:1 (WCAG AA): it is the main color when that is enough, or a darker (light theme) or lighter (dark theme) shade of it; data-mtx-contrast="mui" restores MUI’s exact values (see Color contrast). If you change a main co

Dark tokens are declared with the [data-mtx-theme='dark'] attribute selector, not only on:root. That’s why you can darken a specific section: Apply Add class="mtx-root" to the container so it paints its own background and text color. Known limitations: There is no selector to switch back to light. There is no [data-mtx-theme='light']: a light section inside a dark page does not get the light values back. Derived tokens. Tokens defined from other tokens on:root are resolved on:root, and the container inherits the already computed value. This affects --mtx-focus-ring-color (follows the primary of <html>), --mtx-type-* (follow the --mtx-font-family of <html>) and --mtx-chip-bg-hover. To change them in a container, redeclare the derived token too. Floating layers. Select and Menu menus are mounted in a portal under <body> ( #mtx-portal), and the Drawer and DateTimePicker backdrops also hang off <body>. Those layers take the theme of <html> / <body>, not the container’s. For a complete theme with no surprises, put data-mtx-theme on <html>.

Save the file (for example materix-theme.css) and load it after the library stylesheet, so its tokens win over the defaults: The:root block holds the light palette, shape and font; the [data-mtx-theme="dark"] block only overrides the palette for the dark theme. Every other token (text, background, action states, elevation…) is described in Theming and customization. Contrast warnings Warnings only appear in Exact MUI mode (or with colors where neither white nor dark text reaches 4.5:1). A warning on the contained text means white or dark text on the main color is below 4.5:1 (MUI’s own warning and info defaults are in that case). d: What Materix UI guarantees for accessibility, what you need to provide, and which keys each interactive component supports.

s.x: Materix starts from native HTML and adds ARIA only where HTML falls short. The library handles the mechanics (roles, states, focus, keyboard); you provide the content (accessible names, text and page structure).

Components are built on the right element: <button> for Button, IconButton and Fab; <input type="checkbox"> for Checkbox and Switch; <input type="radio"> for Radio; <input>, <textarea> and <select> for fields; <table> for Table. That’s why they work with forms, native validation, autofill and screen readers with no extra work. When the element is not natively interactive (a <div> such as a clickable Chip, CardActionArea or TableSortLabel), the library adds role="button", tabindex="0" and activation with Enter and Space.

Component ARIA applied by the library TextField aria-invalid on error, aria-describedby pointing to the helper text and counter, aria-live="polite" on the counter, automatic id to link the <label>. Select role="combobox" + aria-expanded, aria-required, aria-invalid, aria-describedby; role="listbox" menu with role="option" and aria-selected; aria-multiselectable in multiple mode. NativeSelect aria-invalid on error. Checkbox aria-checked="mixed" in the indeterminate state. Switch role="switch" on the native checkbox. Tabs role="tablist", role="tab" with aria-selected and roving tabindex, role="tabpanel", aria-orientation when vertical. Menu role="menu", role="menuitem"; on the trigger, aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls. Dialog role="dialog", aria-modal="true"; copies aria-labelledby and aria-describedby from the container to the paper. Drawer role="dialog" in temporary mode; navigation or region in persistent/permanent mode; aria-expanded and aria-controls on the triggers. Alert role="alert". Snackbar role="alert" on the message (configurable with data-role). Table aria-sort on the sorted column, aria-selected on selected rows, aria-live="polite" on the pagination

Visible focus. Inside.mtx-root, every keyboard-focused element shows a --mtx-focus-ring-width (2px) ring in --mtx-focus-ring-color. Text fields don’t use it: they indicate focus with their outline or underline, as in MUI. Focus trap. Dialog and the temporary Drawer keep Tab inside the panel while they are open. Initial focus. Dialog focuses the element marked with data-dialog-autofocus or, if there is none, the first focusable element. Focus restoration. When Dialog, Menu (with Esc), Select (with Esc) and SpeedDial (with Esc) close, focus returns to the element that opened them.

Every floating or modal surface (Dialog, temporary Drawer, Popover, Menu and submenus, Select, Autocomplete, DateTimePicker, SpeedDial, Backdrop, Snackbar and Tooltip) joins a shared layer stack ( src/core/layers.js) when it opens and leaves it when it closes. A single keydown listener on document delivers Escape only to the top layer and marks the event as handled ( preventDefault() plus an internal flag), so the layers below ignore it: Order. The last surface opened is the top one: a popover opened inside a dialog closes before the dialog, a submenu before its menu, a dialog opened from a popover before the popover. Tooltips first. If a tooltip is visible, Escape hides it first and only it (WCAG 1.4.13, dismissible). Tooltips never block the other layers: they don’t count for focus trapping or “click outside”. Snackbars last. A snackbar only receives Escape when no other layer is open. Non-dismissible layers. A Dialog or Drawer with data-disable-escape, or a Backdrop that locks the page ( data-lock-scroll / data-inert) without data-close-on-escape, consumes Escape without closing, so nothing underneath closes either. Click outside. Interacting with a layer opened from another one
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, base.css shortens every animation and transition of Materix elements ( mtx-* classes) to 0.01ms, and the ripple and JavaScript-driven transitions don’t run.

Accessibility is a priority of Materix UI, so every color meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text) by default. MUI’s default palette doesn’t in some combinations: warning (#ed6c02) and info (#0288d1) as text on white or with white text on top, and error with white text in dark mode, stay between 3.0 and 3.9:1. MUI itself recommends raising contrastThreshold to 4.5 to reach AA; Materix ships that choice as the default, the equivalent of createTheme({ palette: { contrastThreshold: 4.5 } }). Brand backgrounds don’t change (warning, info and error keep MUI’s colors in contained buttons, filled chips, badges and alerts): only the text colors do, through the --mtx-color-{color}-text and --mtx-color-{color}-contrast tokens. To get MUI’s exact values (for example, to match an existing MUI app pixel by pixel), opt out with data-mtx-contrast="mui": The attribute works on <html> or on any container, and combines with light and dark themes (also when one of them is set on a nested container). data-mtx-contrast="aa" is still accepted as an alias of the default (useful to return to AA inside a mui container). d: Choose the language of Materix UI's built-in strings per page, per container or per component, override individual strings and register new languages.

s.x: Materix translates the strings it generates itself: the DateTimePicker buttons and month names, the Select search box and counters, and the TablePagination labels. Your own text (labels, helper text, content) is yours to write in whatever language you want. Two languages ship out of the box: en (English, the default) and es (Spanish).

For each component, Materix uses the first registered language it finds, in this order: data-locale, data-lang or lang on the element itself or on its closest ancestor that has one of those attributes ( <html lang> does not count at this step; data-locale / data-lang on <html> do). The global language set explicitly with setLocale(). The lang attribute of <html>. en. Regional codes are reduced to their base language: es-MX and es-ES resolve to es. Until you call setLocale(), <html lang> determines the language of the whole page: setLocale() overrides <html lang>, not a local lang On a page with <html lang="es">, Materix.setLocale('en') switches the components to English. A lang, data-locale or data-lang on the component or on an ancestor below <html> still wins, so a <section lang="es"> stays in Spanish. resetLocale() discards the explicit language and goes back to following <html lang>.

data-locale on a container or on the component itself forces its language: data-lang is equivalent to data-locale. If the closest ancestor declares an unregistered language (for example lang="fr" without having added fr), Materix skips straight to the explicit global language, then to <html lang> and finally to en. In the DateTimePicker, use the two-letter code in data-locale ( es, not es-MX). The picker reads that attribute as is, and a regional code on its own element falls back to English.

setLocale() changes the global language and dispatches mtx:locale:change on document (the deprecated alias mtx:localechange is still dispatched until 1.0). DateTimePicker, Select and TablePagination listen for it and re-render their strings: setLocale() takes precedence over <html lang>, so it is enough on its own. Keeping <html lang> in sync is still good practice for screen readers and the browser: Listen for the same event to update your own strings:

s.h: Overriding a string on a component
s.x: data-* attributes take precedence over any dictionary. Use them to change a specific string without changing the language: Component Attribute String it replaces DateTimePicker data-ok-text OK button. data-cancel-text Cancel button. data-today-text Today button. Select data-none-results-text (alias data-no-results-text) No search results. {0} is the search term. data-select-all-text Select all button ( data-actions-box). data-deselect-all-text (alias data-clear-all-text) Deselect all button. data-placeholder Text shown with no selection (has no default translation). TablePagination data-label-rows-per-page “Rows per page:”. data-label-all “All” option. data-label-of “of” in “1–10 of 100”. data-label-more-than “more than” when the total is unknown. data-label-first, data-label-previous, data-label-next, data-label-last aria-label of the navigation buttons.

addLocale(code, dictionary) registers a new language (or replaces an entire one). Missing keys fall back to English, so you can start with just the ones you need: Register the language before the components that use it are initialized, or call setLocale() afterwards so they update.

updateLocale(code, partial) deep-merges the keys you pass and keeps the rest. If the language doesn’t exist, it creates it: Components that have already rendered don’t update on their own after updateLocale: call Materix.setLocale(Materix.getLocale()) to dispatch mtx:locale:change.

d: Complete, responsive pages built only with Materix UI components. Open the live preview, copy the HTML and adapt it to your project.

s.x: Each template is a single, self-contained index.html file inside the /templates folder of the repository. It uses the real library, so what you see in the preview is exactly what you get. Open the Live preview to try it, or Source code to read it. Copy the HTML into your project. Page-specific styles live in a <style> block with tpl-{slug}-* classes built on --mtx-* tokens, and the interactivity in a short <script> at the end of the <body>. Point the <link> and <script> tags to your copy of Materix UI (or to a CDN) and replace the sample content with your own.

materix.min.css and materix.umd.js from the dist/ folder (or a CDN). The Roboto and Material Icons fonts from Google Fonts. templates/shared/template.js (optional): light/dark theme switching. If you don’t copy it, remove the theme button or wire it to your own logic.
All templates support both themes. Use the theme button in each template or add?theme=dark (or?theme=light) to the URL to force one, for example sign-in/index.html?theme=dark.
Templates are released under the MIT license, like the rest of Materix UI: you can use them in personal and commercial projects, modify them and redistribute them.

A 12-column flexbox grid with five breakpoints (xs–xl), gap-based spacing in multiples of 8px (also per breakpoint) and alignment, for responsive layouts.

s.x: Grid splits the available width into 12 columns and lets each item declare how many it spans at each breakpoint, just like MUI’s Grid (v2: flexbox with gap, no negative margins). Use it to lay out pages, forms and dashboards that change their number of columns with the screen width. To stack elements in a single direction with a fixed gap you don’t need a grid: use Stack; to center and cap the page width, Container.

A data-mtx="grid" container with data-spacing and, inside it, data-mtx="grid" items with the number of columns per breakpoint ( data-xs, data-sm, data-md, data-lg, data-xl). An element with any data-{breakpoint} becomes an item; with none, a container. xs=12 sm=6 md=3 xs=12 sm=6 md=3 xs=12 sm=6 md=3 xs=12 sm=6 md=3
Each item spans n/12 of the width: data-xs="6" is half, data-xs="4" a third. If a row adds up to more than 12, the items wrap onto the next line. xs=8 xs=4 xs=4 xs=8

Breakpoints are mobile-first: a value applies from that width upward until a larger breakpoint overrides it. If you only set data-md="6", the item has no fixed width below 900px (it fits its content); always declare data-xs as the base. Breakpoint Attribute Minimum width Typical device xs data-xs 0px Mobile sm data-sm 600px Portrait tablet md data-md 900px Landscape tablet and small laptop lg data-lg 1200px Desktop xl data-xl 1536px Wide monitor A B C D E F

data-spacing="n" separates rows and columns by n × 8px using CSS gap, like MUI Grid v2. There are no negative margins or item paddings, so the grid never overflows its parent and needs no overflow: hidden wrapper. Each column width subtracts its proportional share of the gap ( 100% · n/12 − gap · (12 − n)/12), so 12 columns always add up to 100%. Any integer from 0 to 12 is valid ( n × --mtx-spacing-unit, 8px by default), plus the half steps of the utilities scale 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 (4, 12 and 20px; they can also be written 0_5, 1_5, 2_5, which is the class suffix). 0 0 0 16px 16px 16px 32px 32px 32px 56px 56px 56px 4px 4px 4px 12px 12px 12px 20px 20px 20px
data-row-spacing and data-column-spacing set each axis separately and override data-spacing on that axis. A B C D
Add -{bp} to any of the three attributes ( data-spacing-md, data-row-spacing-lg, data-column-spacing-sm …). Like the columns, the value applies from that breakpoint up. 1 2 3 4

true makes the item grow to share the remaining space equally with the other growing items. auto sizes the item to the width of its content ( flex: 0 0 auto), like MUI’s size="auto". You can mix both with fixed columns. true true true true xs=6 true auto: fits its content true: takes the rest auto

On the container, data-justify aligns along the main axis, data-align along the cross axis and data-direction changes the flow direction. center center short tall short 1 2 3 data-justify: flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, space-around, space-evenly. data-align: flex-start, center, flex-end, stretch, baseline. data-direction: row, row-reverse, column, column-reverse. Line wrapping is controlled with the mtx-grid--wrap-wrap, mtx-grid--wrap-nowrap and mtx-grid--wrap-reverse classes (there’s no data-* attribute). No offsets or ordering Materix doesn’t include offsets ( offset) or per-breakpoint ordering. To push columns, use data-justify on the container or an empty item of the desired width; to reverse the order, data-direction="row-reverse".
An item can also be a container: add data-container next to its columns and define another 12-column grid inside it. nested 6 nested 6 nested 12 md=4

Variable Description --mtx-spacing-unit Spacing unit (8px). data-spacing="n" produces a gap of n × --mtx-spacing-unit. --mtx-grid-parent-column-spacing Internal: the parent’s horizontal gap, set on each direct child so column widths can subtract it. Don’t set it by hand.

The grid is purely visual: it adds no roles and doesn’t change semantics. Use meaningful elements ( <main>, <section>, <form>) for the blocks you lay out. Reading and tab order follow the HTML, not the visual position. With data-direction="row-reverse" or column-reverse the visual order is reversed but the keyboard order isn’t: only use them when the order doesn’t matter. Check that the content remains readable at a width of 320px (WCAG 1.4.10): always set data-xs so the columns stack on mobile.

d: Materix global baseline: Roboto typography, theme background and text colors, box-sizing, visible focus and a light or dark color-scheme.

s.x: CssBaseline marks a root element with the mtx-root class, which enables the Materix style baseline: Roboto typography at 16px, the theme’s background and text colors, box-sizing: border-box across the whole tree, an accessible focus ring and a color-scheme consistent with the light or dark theme. Use it only once, on your application’s <body>, or on a container if Materix lives alongside other styles. It isn’t a full reset: it doesn’t remove heading or list margins, nor does it normalize forms.

Add data-mtx="css-baseline" to the <body>. The component adds the mtx-root class; writing class="mtx-root" directly produces the same result without JavaScript. Equivalence <body data-mtx="css-baseline"> and <body class="mtx-root"> are equivalent. The class is preferable if you want to avoid a visual jump before the JavaScript loads.

All rules come from src/styles/base.css and are scoped to.mtx-root and its descendants. The reduced-motion rule only touches Materix elements ( mtx-* classes). Selector Properties Effect.mtx-root,.mtx-root *,::before,::after box-sizing: border-box Padding and border are included in the width. body.mtx-root margin: 0 Removes the margin of the <body>. A scoped container keeps its own margin..mtx-root font-family: var(--mtx-font-family); font-weight: 400; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5 Base Roboto typography (equivalent to body1)..mtx-root color: var(--mtx-color-text-primary); background-color: var(--mtx-color-background-default) Text and background colors of the active theme..mtx-root color-scheme: light Light native controls, scrollbars and autofill..mtx-root[data-mtx-theme='dark'], [data-mtx-theme='dark'].mtx-root color-scheme: dark Dark native controls when the theme is dark..mtx-root -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale Font smoothing on macOS..mtx-root strong,.mtx-root b font-weight: 700 True bold with Roboto 700..mtx-root:focus-visible (except input, textarea, select and.mtx-menu) outline: var(--mtx-focus-ring-width) solid var(--mtx-focus-r

The theme is chosen with data-mtx-theme on <html> (or on any ancestor). The tokens change and.mtx-root adopts the matching background, text and color-scheme, so native controls ( <input type="date">, scrollbars) also look dark. Text with the base typography and bold at 700. Native option Switch this page’s theme to see how the native date picker and <select> follow the color-scheme.

CssBaseline can be applied to a container instead of the <body>, for example when embedding a Materix widget in a page with other styles. Only that subtree receives the typography, colors and box-sizing. Widget with baseline This block uses Roboto, the background-default background and the Materix focus ring. Action Scope A scoped container keeps its margin (only body.mtx-root gets margin: 0). The prefers-reduced-motion rule only reduces the animations of elements with mtx-* classes; the rest of the page keeps its own.
There’s no inner structure: the class is enough.
With ES modules:

Attribute Values Default Description data-mtx css-baseline — Adds the mtx-root class to the element. data-mtx-theme light, dark light On <html> or an ancestor (not a component attribute): selects the theme and the color-scheme.
Class Description mtx-root Enables the baseline described in “What it applies” for the element and its descendants.
CssBaseline doesn’t expose its own methods.
CssBaseline doesn’t emit events.

Variable Usage --mtx-font-family Base font family. --mtx-color-text-primary Text color. --mtx-color-background-default Background color. --mtx-focus-ring-width, --mtx-focus-ring-color:focus-visible ring.

The focus ring only appears with the keyboard (:focus-visible) and has a 2px offset so it doesn’t cover the content. Text fields are excluded because they already indicate focus with their border. color-scheme makes native controls and scrollbars respect the contrast of the dark theme. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the animations and transitions of Materix elements are reduced to 0.01ms. The baseline doesn’t change semantics: keep using real headings, lists and landmarks.

s.x: Container is the most basic layout block: it centers its content horizontally, caps it at a max width and adds side padding (gutters) that grows with the screen, just like MUI’s Container. Use it to wrap <main>, landing page sections or a toolbar. To split columns inside it use Grid; to stack blocks, Stack.

When content needs columns that line up across rows, use Grid; for standalone flex helpers, see the utilities guide.

d: Action button with text, outlined and contained variants, three canonical heights (48/40/32px), palette colors and icons.

s.x: Button lets users take an action or confirm a decision with a single click: submit a form, open a dialog, send a message. Use it when the action has a text label that describes it. If the action can only be represented by an icon, use Icon Button; if it’s the primary, persistent action of the whole screen, use a Fab. To navigate to another page, render the button as an <a href> link. Button, Icon Button or Fab? Component When to use it Example Button Action with a text label; hierarchy through the variant. “Save”, “Cancel” Icon Button Compact action recognizable by its icon, in toolbars or rows. Search, close, more options Fab The primary action of the screen, floating above the content. Compose email, create event

A single <button> with the variant class and data-mtx="button". The library adds the ripple effect and handles the disabled state; there’s no inner structure to write. Save Preview Cancel Button has no data-variant: the variant is chosen with classes ( mtx-button--contained, --outlined, --text). The color accepts the class ( mtx-button--error) or data-color, the size data-size and the icons data-start-icon / data-end-icon.

Visual hierarchy is expressed through the variant, just like in MUI: Contained ( mtx-button--contained): high emphasis, filled and elevated. Reserved for the primary action; ideally one per block. Outlined ( mtx-button--outlined): medium emphasis, for important secondary actions. Text ( mtx-button--text): low emphasis, for actions in dialogs, cards or next to a contained button. Contained Outlined Text

Three canonical heights with data-size. Medium (40px) is the default and matches the height of a small Text Field, so both line up in the same row. Hover, visible focus (when navigating with Tab) and press (ripple) are applied automatically. To disable a button, use the native disabled attribute: it dims the button, removes it from the tab order and blocks the ripple. Contained Outlined Text

With data-loading the button enters a loading state like MUI’s loading: it gets disabled ( disabled, or aria-disabled on <a>), receives aria-busy="true" and shows a decorative 16px CircularProgress in the text color. data-loading-position picks the position: center (default; the label becomes transparent and the width doesn’t change), start or end (they replace the start or end icon, including the one generated by data-start-icon / data-end-icon, without changing the width; without an icon, the indicator is added on that side). data-loading-indicator shows a text instead of the spinner. Always use <button> for actions and <a href> for navigation; don’t use <div role="button">. Icon-only buttons ( mtx-button--icon) need an aria-label. Icons next to text have aria-hidden="true" (including the ones generated by data-start-icon / data-end-icon). disabled removes the button from the tab order. On links, disable() applies aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="-1", and blocks the click. While loading, the button is disabled with aria-busy="true" and keeps its accessible name (with center the label only becomes transparent). The indicator is aria-hidden; to announce progress, use your own aria-live region. The ripple respects prefers-reduced-motion. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves focus to the next / previous button. d: Groups related buttons into a single piece with joined borders, separators and inherited variant, size and color.

s.x: Button Group joins several related Buttons into a single piece: shared borders, separators between buttons and a single variant, size and color. Use it for sibling actions (copy / cut / paste, previous / next) or for the split button pattern. If the buttons represent a selection (active alignment, list or grid view), use Toggle Button, which manages the pressed state.

A container with data-mtx="button-group" and plain buttons inside: the group turns them into Buttons, applies its variant ( outlined by default) and adds role="group". Give it an accessible name with data-label or aria-label. One Two Three

The container gets role="group" (unless it already has a role or is a <fieldset>); name it with data-label or aria-label so screen readers announce the purpose of the set. Each child is a native <button> (or <a>): tab order is the natural one, without roving tabindex. Tab moves through the buttons and Enter / Space activate them. Vertical groups keep role="group" without aria-orientation (not allowed on that role, as in MUI). d: Circular icon-only button for compact actions in toolbars, cards and table rows. Always with an aria-label.

s.x: Icon Button triggers an action represented solely by a recognizable icon: search, close, share, open a menu. It is the right choice in toolbars, card headers and per-row actions, where space is limited. If the icon is not unambiguous, use a Button with text; if it is the primary action of the screen, use a Fab. aria-label is required An Icon Button has no visible text: without aria-label (or aria-labelledby) screen readers would only announce “button”. Describe the action, not the icon: “Delete invoice”, not “trash can”.
An empty <button> with data-mtx="icon-button" and data-icon. The library adds the mtx-icon-button class, injects the Material Icons glyph (24px, with aria-hidden="true") and the centered ripple.

Three sizes via data-size. The icon always keeps its native 24px grid (it is never rescaled); what changes is the touch target. You can set the icon with data-icon or write it inside the button (useful for Material Symbols or another icon family). If the button already has content, data-icon is ignored. An <svg> inside the button renders at 24 × 24px with currentColor (MUI’s native grid). As an <a>, the button is not underlined.

Without data-color the icon uses the active action gray ( --mtx-color-action-active), as in MUI. data-color accepts any palette color, or inherit to take the color of the surrounding text. data-color="inherit" is the option for dark or colored surfaces (AppBar, banners): the icon takes the container’s color. Hover shows a subtle background, keyboard focus a ring in the primary color, and a press a centered ripple. Disable it with the native disabled attribute.

data-edge="start|end" (or the mtx-icon-button--edge-start and mtx-icon-button--edge-end classes) apply a negative 12px margin so the glyph is optically aligned with the content edge, like MUI’s edge prop. Use them on the first or last item of a bar. Inbox

Wrap the Icon Button in a Badge to show counters. Include the number in the aria-label. The button does not clip its content (the ripple is clipped by an inner container), so the badge can also sit inside the button.

An icon alone is not always self-explanatory. Add data-mtx-tooltip to show its name on hover, keyboard focus or long press (see Tooltip); no initialization required. If the button has no aria-label, the tooltip text becomes its accessible name; if it already has one, the tooltip is linked as a description ( aria-describedby). Recommended for icon-only buttons MUI recommends wrapping every icon-only button in a Tooltip. With Materix it is one attribute: data-mtx-tooltip="Action". A disabled button does not receive pointer events: wrap it in <span data-mtx="tooltip" data-title="…">.

d: Floating action button for a screen's primary action: circular (56/48/40px) or extended with text (48px).

s.x: Fab (Floating Action Button) represents the primary or most common action on a screen —compose, create, add— and floats above the content with high elevation. Use at most one per screen. For secondary actions use a Button; for compact actions in toolbars or rows, an Icon Button.
An empty <button> with data-mtx="fab" and data-icon generates a circular FAB; adding data-label turns it into an extended FAB with text. The circular FAB needs an aria-label.

Circular (default): icon only, 56px. Extended ( mtx-fab--extended): icon and text, 48px tall. It’s enabled automatically with data-label, or with data-variant="extended" if you write the content yourself. Use the extended FAB when the icon alone isn’t clear enough.

With data-size. Unlike Button, the FAB’s default size is large. Size data-size Circular Extended Aligns with Large — (default) 56px 48px Medium Text Field (56px) Medium medium 48px 40px Large Button, large Icon Button Small small 40px 34px Medium Button, small Text Field

Combine data-icon and data-label depending on what you want to convey: icon only, icon and text, or text only. The generated icon is decorative ( aria-hidden="true"); the data-label text is the accessible name of the extended FAB.
Primary is the default. data-color accepts the palette colors and default, a neutral surface with a border, useful when the screen already has a lot of primary color.
On hover and focus the elevation rises from 6 to 12; with the keyboard a focus ring also appears. With the disabled attribute it loses its color and shadow.

Positioning utility classes: mtx-fab--fixed-br / mtx-fab--fixed-bl: fixed 24px from the bottom-right / bottom-left corner of the window. mtx-fab--absolute-center: horizontally centered and straddling the top edge of its positioned container (for example, a bottom bar). A fixed FAB covers content at the end of the page: leave a bottom margin of at least 88px (56px + 24px + some slack) in the scrolling container.
Composing a message: the send FAB (56px) aligned with a medium Text Field of the same height.

It’s a native <button>. The circular FAB needs an aria-label; the extended FAB takes its name from its text. Place it at a sensible point in the reading order: even though it floats visually, its position in the DOM determines the tab order. disabled removes it from the tab order. d: A box for selecting one or more options from a list or confirming a condition; supports an indeterminate state.

s.x: Checkbox lets users select zero, one or several options from a set, or confirm a condition (“I accept the terms”). It keeps a native <input type="checkbox">, so it works in forms, with the keyboard and with screen readers without extra code. If the option applies a change immediately, use a Switch; if only one option can be chosen, use Radio. Checkbox, Switch or Radio? Component When to use it Checkbox Several independent options, or a confirmation applied when a form is submitted. Switch Turning a preference on/off with an immediate effect, without a “Save” button. Radio Choosing exactly one option from a small, visible group.

Write just the input with data-mtx="checkbox" and data-label. The library wraps it in a <label class="mtx-checkbox">, draws the box and the label, and keeps id, name, value, checked, required and the rest of the attributes.
Two sizes, as in MUI: medium (18px box, default) and small (16px with 14px text) via data-size="small", for tables and dense forms.
Without data-label, only the box is drawn. In that case give it an accessible name with aria-label or aria-labelledby, for example in a table’s selection column.
Primary is the default. Use data-color on the input ( secondary, success, error, warning, info) or the mtx-checkbox--{color} class, which is appended to the generated container.

Unchecked, checked and indeterminate, each enabled or with disabled. Hover colors the border, pressing shows a ripple centered on the box and keyboard focus shows a ring. For a validation error use data-error (or setError()): it sets aria-invalid, paints the border red and shows the message linked with aria-describedby (see Helper and error text): The native <input type="checkbox"> doesn’t support readonly. To show a checkbox the user can’t change, use disabled.

data-helper-text wraps the checkbox in.mtx-form-control and adds a.mtx-form-helper-text below it, linked with aria-describedby. An empty data-error turns on the error while keeping the helper text; with text, the message replaces it. The input gets aria-invalid="true" and the unchecked border turns red. From code: setError(), clearError() and setHelperText()..mtx-form-helper-text also works with CSS only (or with data-mtx="form-helper-text", which adds an id). If you write the wrapper by hand, the control links the existing helper automatically: Subscribe to the newsletter One email a month, no spam. The indeterminate state indicates that only some of the child options are checked (the “select all” pattern). It’s declared with data-indeterminate or the indeterminate property, and the library syncs aria-checked="mixed". It’s purely visual: on click, the browser clears it and applies checked/unchecked.

The native input stays in the DOM: it keeps form submission, required and checkbox semantics. The whole row ( <label>) is clickable. d: Radio button to choose exactly one option from a visible group; RadioGroup reads and sets the group's value.

s.x: Radio lets the user choose exactly one option from a small set where it helps to see all the alternatives at once (plan, shipping method, frequency). Each option is a native <input type="radio">, so mutual exclusion by name, arrow-key navigation and form submission work with no extra code. RadioGroup is the optional container that stacks the options and exposes the selected value. Radio, Select, Checkbox or Switch? You need… Use A single option out of 2 to ~6, all visible Radio A single option out of many, or little space Select / Native Select Several independent options Checkbox To turn a single preference on or off Switch
Each option is written as a single input with data-mtx="radio", data-label and the same name. Wrap them in data-mtx="radio-group" to stack them and read the group’s value.
Two sizes: medium (20px circle, default) and small (16px with 14px text) with data-size="small".
The group is vertical by default, the easiest layout to scan. With data-row="true" the options are laid out in a row (wrapping if they don’t fit). Use it with few, short options.
Primary is the default. Use data-color on the input ( secondary, success, error, warning, info) or the mtx-radio--{color} class, which is appended to the generated container.

Hover colors the border, a press shows a centered ripple and keyboard focus a ring. disabled dims the option and excludes it from arrow-key navigation. For a validation error use data-error on the group (or group.setError()): the radiogroup gets aria-invalid="true", the unchecked circles and the label turn red, and the message is linked with aria-describedby. data-helper-text adds a permanent hint: The native <input type="radio"> does not support readonly. To lock the choice, use disabled.

Every group needs an accessible name. The simplest way is data-label on the group: it generates a.mtx-form-label and links it with aria-labelledby. <fieldset> + <legend> or your own aria-label / aria-labelledby also work. RadioGroup adds role="radiogroup" automatically (unless the container already declares another role).
Shipping method at checkout: a few mutually exclusive options with information worth comparing. Shipping method
For SSR or fine-grained control, declare each <label class="mtx-radio"> with its input, circle and label, and the group with its classes.

Get the RadioGroup instance with Materix.getInstance(container). It exposes value (read and write) and emits mtx:radio-group:change when the user changes the selection. Each Radio is retrieved with Materix.getInstance(input). With ES modules: RadioGroup is exported as Materix.RadioGroup ( new Materix.RadioGroup(el)), in addition to the declarative data-mtx="radio-group" or Materix.init(el, 'radio-group'). It exposes value, disable() / enable(), setError(), clearError() and setHelperText(). group.value = 'high'

Written on the input (simplified syntax) or on the <label> (BEM). Preserved native attributes: id, name, value, checked, disabled, required, aria-*.

Native inputs are grouped by name: the browser handles mutual exclusion, roving focus and arrow keys. RadioGroup adds role="radiogroup" automatically; name it with data-label, <fieldset> / <legend> or aria-labelledby. The radio relies on its native state (no aria-checked is added). The whole row is clickable; without data-label, use an aria-label on each input. Key Action Tab Enters the group (on the selected option) or leaves it. ↓ / → Selects the next option. ↑ / ← Selects the previous option. Space Selects the focused option if it is not already selected.

d: Star rating to review a product or display an average score, accessible through native radios and the keyboard.

s.x: Rating lets the user pick a score from 1 to N icons (stars by default) or displays an average in read-only mode. As in MUI, it is backed by hidden native radios with labels (“3 Stars”), so it works with the keyboard, screen readers and forms without extra JavaScript. For a long numeric scale use a Select or a number field.
A single <span data-mtx="rating"> renders five stars. data-value sets the initial value and data-name the radios’ name (submitted with the form). Clicking the current value clears it.
data-precision="0.5" allows half stars: each star contains two radios and its left half picks the x.5 value. Fractions such as 0.25 also work.

MUI sizes through data-size: small 18px, medium 24px (default) and large 30px. Icons and size The built-in icons ( star, star_border, star_outline, favorite, favorite_border, thumb_up, thumb_up_off_alt, circle, radio_button_unchecked) are drawn as SVG, which scales without losing sharpness. Any other name uses the Material Icons glyph at its native 24px in every size: its font-size is never forced (Materix iconography rule).
data-icon (filled) and data-empty-icon (empty) accept Material Icons names. If you only set data-icon, the empty state uses the same icon in gray. Customize the color with --mtx-rating-color.
Hovering previews the value (the active star grows 1.2×); with Tab and the arrow keys it changes with a visible focus ring. data-read-only displays a fixed rating and data-disabled dims it.
data-highlight-selected-only highlights only the chosen icon (satisfaction scales) and data-max changes the number of icons.
mtx:rating:active reports the value under the pointer (or null on leave) so you can show a descriptive label, like MUI’s hover feedback demo.
A product summary with the read-only average and a review form that submits the value like any other radio. 4.5 · 1,284 reviews Your rating Submit
For SSR you can write the generated structure: one.mtx-rating__item per icon with its hidden radio and its <label> carrying data-rating-value. The library reuses the nodes and adds any missing icons.

Materix.getInstance(el) returns the Rating: value (a number or null) can be read and written without firing events, and mtx:rating:change reports user changes. With ES modules: rating.value = 5 rating.value = null

Not fired when value is set from code. mtx:rating:active (bubbles) { value: number | null } The value under the pointer changes ( null on leave). change (native, on the radio) — The user checks a radio.

Interactive: native radios sharing a name, each with a translated label (“1 Star”, “3 Stars”; “3 estrellas” in Spanish) plus an “Empty” radio. The browser handles mutual exclusion and the arrow keys. When the container has a name ( aria-label, aria-labelledby or data-label) it gets role="radiogroup". Read-only: role="img" with a translated aria-label (“Rated 4 out of 5” / “Valoración: 4 de 5”); the icons are decorative. Keyboard focus is shown as a ring around the focused icon. Key Action Tab Enters the rating (on the checked value) or leaves it. → / ↑ Increases the value by one precision step (reversed in RTL). ← / ↓ Decreases the value; below the minimum it moves to “Empty”.

d: Lets users pick a value or a range by dragging along a track, built on accessible native range inputs.

s.x: Slider lets the user select a value (or a range) from a continuous or stepped scale: volume, brightness, price filters, temperatures. As in MUI, every thumb is backed by a visually hidden native <input type="range">, so the keyboard, screen readers and form submission work without extra code. For an exact number the user must type, use a Text Field with type="number"; for a few discrete options, use a Toggle Button group or Radio buttons.
A single <input type="range" data-mtx="slider"> builds the rail, track, thumb and value label. min, max, step, value and name are kept on the native input, and data-label sets the accessible name.
Two sizes, as in MUI: medium (4px rail, 20px thumb) and small (2px rail, 12px thumb without shadow).
The slider fills the available width, so decorative icons go next to it inside a horizontal Stack (MUI’s “Volume” pattern).
data-color accepts the MUI palette: primary, secondary, error, warning, info and success.
Hovering the thumb shows an 8px halo, keyboard focus shows the same halo and dragging grows it to 14px (pressed). data-disabled renders the slider in grey and blocks interaction.

The value label is a Material Design 2 teardrop balloon. data-value-label-display is off (default), auto (on hover, focus and drag) or on (always visible). data-value-label-format replaces {value} with the localized number and is also used as aria-valuetext.

data-marks="true" adds a mark at every step; a "value:label,…" list adds labelled marks (a JSON array [{"value":0,"label":"0 °C"}] also works). With data-marks-only the value can only land on a mark, like MUI’s step={null}.

As in MUI, each mark label is centered on its mark, so the labels at min and max overflow the rail by half their width. In narrow containers (cards, side panels, 390px phones) add data-marks-inset: the first label aligns to the start of the rail and the last one to the end (bottom/top in vertical, mirrored in RTL), while the intermediate labels stay centered.

data-range with data-value="20,60" creates two thumbs, each with its own native input named {name}-start and {name}-end and labelled “Minimum” / “Maximum”. When the thumbs cross they swap, as in MUI; data-disable-swap blocks them and data-min-distance enforces a minimum gap. Form submission A range slider submits two fields: price-start and price-end for name="price". In the full BEM syntax you write both inputs yourself and keep their names.
data-track is normal (default), inverted (highlights the part after the value) or false (no track, useful with marks).
data-orientation="vertical" grows from bottom to top (200px by default; change it with --mtx-slider-vertical-length). The native input gets aria-orientation="vertical".
Inside a dir="rtl" container the value grows from right to left and the left arrow key increases it.
A price filter that syncs a summary while dragging ( mtx:slider:input) and submits both native inputs. Price (USD) $200 – $700 Apply filter

For SSR you can write the full structure: a.mtx-slider container, rail, track and one.mtx-slider__thumb per input (two for a range). The library reuses the nodes and adds the missing value labels and marks.

Materix.getInstance(el) works with the original input or with the generated.mtx-slider container. value is a number (or [start, end] in range mode) and can be set without firing events. With ES modules: slider.value = 75 disable() enable()
