Variable Use --mtx-slider-color, --mtx-slider-contrast Main color and value label text color (set by data-color). --mtx-slider-thickness, --mtx-slider-thumb-size Rail thickness and thumb size. --mtx-slider-halo Hover/focus/pressed halo color (16% alpha). --mtx-slider-vertical-length Height of a vertical slider (200px). --mtx-slider-label-size Minimum value label size (32px). --mtx-slider-disabled-color Disabled color (grey 400 / grey 600 in dark theme).

Each thumb is a native <input type="range">: the browser exposes role="slider", aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow. With data-value-label-format the component also sets aria-valuetext (“21 °C”). Name it with data-label, aria-label or aria-labelledby. In range mode each thumb gets a translated name: “Price: Minimum” / “Price: Maximum” (“Precio: Mínimo” / “Precio: Máximo” in Spanish). Vertical sliders set aria-orientation="vertical". The value label and marks are decorative ( aria-hidden). The focus indicator is the 8px halo around the thumb; animations are disabled with prefers-reduced-motion. Key Action Tab Moves focus to the thumb (each thumb of a range is a tab stop). → / ↑ Increases by one step (in RTL, ← increases). ← / ↓ Decreases by one step. Page Up / Page Down Increases / decreases by 10% of the range. Home / End Sets the minimum / maximum.

d: Toggle that turns an option on or off instantly, like a settings preference; uses role=switch on a native checkbox.

s.x: Switch turns a single option on or off with immediate effect: Wi-Fi, dark mode, notifications. It is a native <input type="checkbox"> to which the library adds role="switch", so it is announced as “on / off”. If the change only applies when a form is submitted, or there are several options to confirm, use a Checkbox. Switch or Checkbox? Ask yourself whether the user expects to see the effect without pressing “Save”. If the answer is yes, it is a Switch (“Dark mode”). If the value is submitted with a form (“I accept the terms”, “Subscribe to the newsletter”), it is a Checkbox.
Write only the input with data-mtx="switch" and data-label. The library generates the track, the thumb and the label inside a <label class="mtx-switch"> and preserves all of the input’s attributes.
Two sizes, as in MUI: medium (34×20px track, default) and small (28×16px with 14px text) with data-size="small".
Without data-label only the switch is drawn; give it an accessible name with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
Primary is the default. Use data-color on the input ( secondary, success, error, warning, info) or the mtx-switch--{color} class, which is appended to the generated container.

A press shows a ripple over the thumb, and keyboard focus a ring around the track. disabled: dims the control and removes it from the tab order. readonly: the control stays focusable and readable, but the library blocks changes by click or keyboard. Useful for settings managed by an administrator.

data-helper-text adds a.mtx-form-helper-text (FormHelperText) below the switch, linked with aria-describedby; data-error (empty or with a message) turns on the error state with aria-invalid="true". See the matching section in Checkbox.
Group related switches in a <fieldset> with a <legend>. Each switch remains independent. Notifications
A settings panel where each switch applies the change as soon as it is toggled, with no “Save” button.
For SSR or fine-grained control, declare the <label> with the input, the track with its thumb, and the label. The library reuses the nodes and adds role="switch" to the input.
Materix.getInstance() accepts the input or the generated <label>. Changes made from code do not fire events; user interactions emit the input’s native change. With ES modules: toggle()

Written on the input (simplified syntax) or on the <label> (BEM). Attribute Values Default Description data-mtx switch — Enables auto-initialization. data-label text — Creates.mtx-switch__label. label is also accepted. data-size small medium Compact size ( mtx-switch--small). data-small boolean — Shortcut for data-size="small". data-disable-ripple boolean — Disables the ripple. data-color primary | secondary | success | error | warning | info primary Color of the checked state (adds mtx-{component}--{color}). data-helper-text text — Creates a.mtx-form-helper-text below the control inside.mtx-form-control, linked with aria-describedby. data-error text | empty | true — Error state: aria-invalid="true" and red helper text. With text, the message replaces the helper text. Relevant native attributes: checked, disabled, readonly (blocks changes), name, value, aria-*.

Class Description mtx-switch <label> container. mtx-switch__input Invisible, overlaid native input with role="switch" (added by the JS). mtx-switch__track 34×20px track. mtx-switch__thumb 16px thumb that slides when checked. mtx-switch__label Label text. mtx-switch--small 28×16px track and 14px text. mtx-switch--secondary, --success, --error, --warning, --info Color of the checked state. mtx-form-control Generated (or hand-written) wrapper grouping the control and.mtx-form-helper-text; --error / --disabled reflect the state. mtx-form-helper-text / --error Helper or error text (MUI FormHelperText).

Method Returns Description checked (get/set) boolean Checked state. toggle() void Toggles the state unless it is disabled or readonly. disable() / enable() void Toggles the input’s disabled. disabled (getter) boolean Disabled state. focus() void Focuses the input. input (property) HTMLInputElement Native input. setHelperText(text) void Creates or changes the helper text (empty removes it). setError(message?) void Turns on the error state ( aria-invalid); with text, the message replaces the helper text. clearError() void Clears the error and restores the helper text. error (getter) boolean Whether it is in the error state. destroy() void Removes the ripple and read-only listeners. Unlinks the instance: getInstance() then returns undefined.

Switch emits no events of its own. Use the input’s native change event (it bubbles), which only fires on user interaction. Event detail Fired when change (native) — (read event.target.checked) The user turns the switch on or off.

Variable Use in Switch --mtx-switch-track Unchecked track. --mtx-switch-thumb Unchecked thumb. --mtx-switch-track-disabled, --mtx-switch-thumb-disabled Disabled state. --mtx-color-{color} Checked thumb and track (at 50%). --mtx-elevation-2 Thumb shadow. --mtx-color-text-primary, --mtx-color-text-disabled, --mtx-type-body1 Label. --mtx-focus-ring-width, --mtx-focus-ring-color Focus ring. --mtx-sw-color Local variable holding the checked color, for customization.

The input keeps its native semantics and gets role="switch": screen readers announce “switch, on/off”. aria-checked is kept in sync with checked (setter and user changes). The helper text stays outside the <label> (so it is not merged into the accessible name) and is linked with aria-describedby, keeping any existing ids. setError() adds aria-invalid="true" and clearError() removes it (only when the library set it). The whole row is clickable. Without data-label, use aria-label or aria-labelledby. readonly keeps the control focusable and readable without faking a disabled state. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves focus to the next / previous switch. Space Turns the switch on or off (unless readonly or disabled).

d: Text field with a floating label, MUI variants, icons, counters, input masks and validation, declared with a single element.

s.x: TextField lets users enter and edit text in forms: name, email, password, amounts or long comments. It is declared with a single <input> or <textarea>, and Materix builds the floating label, the notched border ( NotchedOutline), the icons and the helper text. To choose from a closed set of options use Select or NativeSelect; for dates and times, use DateTimePicker.

Write only the native element with data-mtx="text-field" and data-label. All native attributes ( id, name, type, value, required, disabled, readonly, maxlength, autocomplete …) are preserved. If you omit data-label, the placeholder text is used as the label. The data-mtx="input" and data-mtx="textarea" aliases initialize the same component.

outlined (default, with border and notch), filled (background and bottom line) and standard (bottom line only). The no-label variant draws a full border with no label or notch, intended for search boxes and filters.

Canonical heights: medium 56px (default, MUI), small 40px ( data-size="small" or data-small) and large 48px ( data-size="large" or data-large). Small lines up 1:1 with a 40px medium Button and large with a 48px large Button. Apply

data-start-icon and data-end-icon accept the name of a Material Icons glyph or an image URL ( http(s)://, /,./,../, data:image/ or a.png,.jpg,.svg,.webp,.gif,.avif or.ico extension). With a start icon, the label shifts to align with the typed text.

They are the equivalent of MUI’s InputAdornment + IconButton. data-password-toggle (only on type="password") adds an end IconButton that shows or hides the password: it toggles aria-pressed, swaps the icon ( visibility / visibility_off) and has a translated accessible name (“Show password”). Masks, the counter and validation keep working. For other actions, data-start-action / data-end-action take the icon name and data-start-action-label / data-end-action-label its accessible name; clicking them fires mtx:text-field:adornment-click. The button’s icon sits exactly where a static icon would, so the label stays aligned with the text. Inside.mtx-text-field, the browser’s native clear button for type="search" (and Edge’s password reveal when there is a password toggle) is hidden, so only the library action is shown. Button label The password button keeps a fixed name and uses aria-pressed for its state (toggle button pattern) instead of changing its text. Override the name with data-password-toggle-label (for example “Show passwords” when the button controls several fields).
data-color changes the color of the label, border and focus line: primary (default), secondary, success, warning and info. Click each field to see it.

States are expressed with native attributes ( disabled, readonly, required) or with data-error: with text ( data-error="message") it paints the field red, replaces the helper text with the message and sets aria-invalid="true"; empty (or "true") it turns on the error while keeping the helper text, like MUI’s boolean error prop. required adds the asterisk to the label. Hover to see the hover state and press Tab for focus.

BEM modifiers applied by putting the class on the <input> itself (it is transferred to the container): mtx-text-field--static-label: the label always stays on top and the placeholder is visible (equivalent to MUI’s shrink). mtx-text-field--hidden-label: hides the label and the notch; add an aria-label. mtx-text-field--borderless: outlined without a border, to integrate the field inside a Paper or a bar.

Use a <textarea> (or data-multiline on an <input>, which is converted into a <textarea>). rows / data-rows sets the initial rows (3 by default). With data-auto-resize the field grows as you type; data-max-rows limits the growth and enables vertical scrolling beyond that number of rows.

data-counter shows a counter in the bottom-right corner: characters, words or both. The data-max-characters (or maxlength) and data-max-words limits trigger the error state when exceeded. If you only set a limit, the counter type is inferred from it. Counter format: n / max with a limit, n (characters) or n words without a limit, and p/max words | c/max chars in both mode. The suffixes follow the component locale ( data-locale, lang or Materix.setLocale()); in Spanish they read n palabras and p/max pal. | c/max car.. Override them with Materix.updateLocale('en', { textField: { counterWords: '{count} words' } }).

d: Date, time, date-time and range pickers with a calendar, MD2 radial clock, popover, modal or static mode, limits and formats.

s.x: DateTimePicker is a single class that covers DatePicker, TimePicker, DateTimePicker and their range versions. It’s declared on an <input>, which becomes a TextField with a mask and an end icon button, and opens a calendar or a clock on click. It follows the WAI-ARIA Date Picker Dialog pattern: an accessible dialog, a keyboard-navigable day grid and a radial clock operable with the arrow keys. Use it when the date or time must be valid and easy to pick; for a date the user knows by heart (e.g. date of birth) a TextField with data-mask="date" may be enough.

The mode is chosen with the value of data-mtx. All TextField attributes ( data-label, data-variant, data-size, data-helper-text, data-start-icon …) work the same way. data-mtx Mode Default end icon Default format ( en · es) date-picker (alias datepicker) Date event MM/DD/YYYY · DD/MM/YYYY time-picker (alias timepicker) Time schedule HH:mm date-time-picker (aliases datetime-picker, datetimepicker) Date and time calendar_month MM/DD/YYYY HH:mm · DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm date-range-picker (alias daterangepicker) Date range event MM/DD/YYYY - MM/DD/YYYY · DD/MM/YYYY - DD/MM/YYYY datetime-range-picker (alias datetimerangepicker) Date-time range calendar_month Date order of the locale + HH:mm date-time-picker (matching the component slug) and datetime-picker are equivalent. data-picker="date|time|datetime" takes precedence over the data-mtx name, e.g. <input data-mtx="date-time-picker" data-picker="date"> is a date-only picker. The field also accepts typing: a mask matching the format is applied, and only digits, separators ( / -.),: and the AM/PM letters are allowed, depending on the mode.
data-variant: outlined (default), filled and standard, inherited from TextField.
Medium 56px (default) and small 40px with data-size="small".

The end icon is rendered as an accessible IconButton ( aria-label="Choose date", aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded) that opens and closes the picker. It’s chosen based on the mode, but you can change it with data-end-icon and add another one with data-start-icon.

Helper text ( data-helper-text), error ( data-error="message"), required ( required), disabled ( disabled) and read-only ( readonly), just like in TextField. With disabled or readonly the calendar button is disabled and the picker can’t be opened; disable() / enable() do the same from JavaScript.

Range modes pick the start and end with two clicks on the same calendar (highlighting the span on hover). In datetime-range-picker, after choosing the dates, start and end time tabs appear. data-range-separator changes the separator ( " - " by default).

The time picker opens in keyboard mode by default (editable hour and minute cards, with ↑ / ↓). With data-time-view="dial" (alias data-time-mode, value clock) it opens the MD2 radial clock; the bottom-left button toggles between the two. data-ampm (or a format with hh / A) enables the 12-hour format with an AM/PM selector.

Popover (default): drops down below the field, anchors to the right or opens upward if there’s not enough room. On screens 600px wide or less it’s shown centered over a dark backdrop. Modal ( data-display="modal"): a centered dialog with an MD2 colored header on any screen size. Static ( data-static on a <div>): a calendar or clock embedded in the page, with no field and no OK/Cancel buttons; each choice emits mtx:date-time-picker:change.

data-min and data-max (or min / max) disable the days outside the interval; they accept YYYY-MM-DD (recommended), the field’s own format or today / hoy. The initial value is set with value, data-value or data-default-value (ISO or the active format); it’s displayed with the active format and the label floats above it from the start.

Without data-format, the date order comes from the locale ( en / en-US: MM/DD/YYYY; es, es-MX, en-GB …: DD/MM/YYYY, resolved with Intl), always with / as separator. data-format defines how the value is displayed and typed (and derives the field mask); typed text is parsed in that same order. Tokens: YYYY / AAAA year, YY short year, MM month, DD day, HH hour 0-23, hh hour 1-12, mm minutes, ss seconds, A AM/PM and a am/pm. If you need a different mask, data-mask replaces it.

The texts (Today, Cancel, OK, accessible names…) come from the Materix i18n system: the locale is resolved with data-locale / data-lang on the field or an ancestor, then with the lang of the ancestor or of <html>, and finally with Materix.setLocale(). Regional codes are reduced to their base language for the texts ( es-MX → es) while the full code is used with Intl (date order and accessible day names). Months and weekdays come from the i18n dictionary when the language is registered ( en, es or one added with Materix.addLocale()) and from Intl.DateTimeFormat otherwise (e.g. fr-FR); an unregistered local locale does not override the text language, which falls back to Materix.setLocale() or <html lang>. data-today-text, data-cancel-text and data-ok-text replace the button texts.

The picker is mounted on the TextField structure. In manual markup, write the complete TextField and put data-mtx on the container; the component generates the popover inside it.

No variables of its own: it uses the global tokens --mtx-color-primary, --mtx-color-primary-contrast, --mtx-color-background-paper, --mtx-color-primary-light, --mtx-color-action-*, --mtx-elevation-*, --mtx-backdrop-bg, --mtx-z-index-modal, --mtx-duration-*, --mtx-easing-*, --mtx-shape-radius and the TextField heights. Range highlights are derived from --mtx-color-primary with color-mix(), so they follow the active theme.

Materix implements the WAI-ARIA Date Picker Dialog pattern: Field: a TextField with <label for>, mask and aria-describedby; typing is still the fastest path. Clicking the field opens the picker without stealing focus; Alt + ↓ (or ↓ when it’s open) moves focus into it. Button: the end icon is a <button> with aria-label="Choose date" (or Choose time, Choose date and time, Choose date range, plus the current value), aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded and aria-controls. It’s disabled together with the field ( disabled / readonly). Dialog: the popover and the modal are role="dialog" with an i18n aria-label; the modal (and the popover on screens ≤ 600px) adds aria-modal="true" and traps focus with Tab. On open, focus goes to the selected day or today; Esc closes and returns focus to the button or field that opened it. In popover mode, tabbing out of the picker closes it. Calendar: role="grid" labelled by the month/year title (an aria-live region), with columnheader cells carrying full weekday names and one row per week. Each day is a gridcell with a full aria-label ( Tuesday, October 20, 2026; martes, 20 de octubre de 2026 with es-MX), aria-selected, aria-current="date" for today and

d: Toggle buttons group related options with exclusive or multiple selection; on their own they work as an on/off switch for a single action.

s.x: Toggle Button groups related options in a block with joined borders: text alignment, formatting, list or grid view. A ToggleButtonGroup handles exclusive selection (like a radio) or multiple selection (like checkboxes), and a standalone ToggleButton switches a single action on and off, such as marking a favorite. To choose among many options use a Select; for a setting that applies immediately, a Switch. aria-label is required on icon-only buttons A button without visible text needs an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) that describes the option: “Align left”, not “arrow”. Also name the group with aria-label or data-label.

A data-mtx="toggle-button-group" container with plain <button> elements. Each button only needs data-value and, when icon-only, data-icon and aria-label; the group initializes the buttons (no data-mtx needed on each one), joins their borders and manages aria-pressed.

With data-exclusive only one button can be active and the value is a string (or null). Without it the selection is multiple (MUI’s default) and the value is an array in DOM order; data-value accepts a comma-separated list.

data-size on the group (or on each button). The icon keeps its native 24px grid; the padding changes (7, 11 and 15px, as in MUI). Every button is a native <button> with aria-pressed (WAI-ARIA toggle button pattern), also in exclusive mode. As in MUI, the group uses role="group" rather than radiogroup: the buttons keep their button semantics, all of them are tabbable and they can be deselected. If you need strict single-choice semantics, use Radio. Name the group with aria-label, aria-labelledby or data-label, and every icon-only button with aria-label. d: Represents a person or entity with an image, initials or an icon; AvatarGroup stacks several and summarizes the overflow.

s.x: Avatar displays the identity of a person or entity in a compact space: a photo, their initials or an icon. Use it in user lists, card headers, comments or app bars. If you need a text label that can be deleted or clicked, use Chip; for a numeric indicator over an icon, use Badge.
A single element with data-mtx="avatar". Write the initials as content, or use data-src for an image and data-icon for a Material Icons icon. RD
data-variant sets the shape: circular (default), rounded (4px radius) or square (no radius). CI RO SQ

There are three canonical sizes: small (24px), medium (40px, default) and large (56px). For one-off cases, data-size also accepts a number in pixels; the font size is computed as 45% of the side. S M L 72 Icons in small avatars Material Icons keep their native 24px grid and are not resized. At the small size (24px) the icon fills the whole avatar; prefer initials for that size.
Content is resolved in this order: a child , then data-src (which generates the , with data-srcset and data-sizes support), then data-icon and, if none of the above is present, the element’s text. CR

Without data-color, the avatar uses a neutral grey ( --mtx-avatar-default-bg) with white text ( --mtx-avatar-default-color). data-color applies any palette color with its contrast text. Deviation from MUI: AA contrast MUI’s default avatar uses grey 400 ( #bdbdbd) with the background color as text, a 1.8:1 contrast that fails WCAG AA. Materix uses grey 600 ( #757575) with white text in both themes (4.6:1, AA). To restore MUI’s look, override --mtx-avatar-default-bg: var(--mtx-color-grey-400) and --mtx-avatar-default-color: var(--mtx-color-background-default). DF PR SE ER WA IN SU

Avatar isn’t interactive: its states are about content. If there’s no image or icon, the avatar enters fallback mode ( mtx-avatar--fallback class) and shows the initials or the element’s text. AG When an image errors, the component hides the broken ( hidden), adds mtx-avatar--fallback and shows the alt text’s first letter (or the element’s text) instead.

Group children The group counts its mtx-avatar children and also the data-mtx="avatar" children that are not initialized yet, so data-max works with the simplified syntax. Icons generated with data-icon have aria-hidden="true". If an icon avatar conveys information, add role="img" and aria-label to the container. Initials are read letter by letter; when they aren’t decorative, add role="img" and aria-label="Full name". AvatarGroup copies data-label to aria-label and gives the +N indicator a label built from data-surplus-label (by default 3 more / 3 más from the i18n dictionary, following the element’s lang; make it specific with something like data-surplus-label="{count} more members"). Overflow avatars are hidden with hidden, so they aren’t announced either. The component isn’t interactive; if an avatar opens a profile, wrap it in an <a> or <button> with an accessible name.

d: Displays a number or a status dot at the corner of an icon, avatar or button to flag new or pending items.

s.x: Badge wraps an element (icon, avatar, button) and places a counter or a dot at its corner. Use it to flag unread messages, pending notifications or an online status. Don’t use it for standalone text labels (use Chip) or for page-level status messages (use Alert).
Wrap the content with data-mtx="badge" and set the value in data-content. The component creates the badge node and positions it.
standard (default) shows the content; dot shows an 8px dot with no text, useful for signaling “there’s something new” without giving a number.

Without data-color (or with default) the badge is an opaque neutral grey that adapts to the light and dark themes ( mtx-badge--default class). The rest of the palette applies its contrast color to the text.
If the content is an integer greater than data-max (99 by default), {max}+ is displayed.

As in MUI, the badge is hidden when the value is 0 or there’s no content. data-show-zero shows the zero and data-invisible always hides it (in the dot variant too). When hidden, it shrinks with a transition without shifting the content.

data-standalone places the badge in the text flow with no anchored element: navigation counters, lists or tabs. With content 0 it disappears completely (unless data-show-zero). Standalone, the number is read as text; data-label ( {0} = displayed content) also adds screen-reader-only text. Inbox
data-anchor places the badge at top-right (default), top-left, bottom-right or bottom-left.
data-overlap="rectangular" (default) anchors the badge to the corners of a box. On circular shapes, such as an avatar, use data-overlap="circular" to bring it closer to the edge of the circle. R C R

An action bar with counters on icon buttons and an avatar with an online status. The number is announced through each button’s aria-label. Badge with IconButton You can place the badge inside the IconButton, wrapping the icon (the MUI pattern), or wrap the button with the badge and data-overlap="circular" so the badge sits on the edge of the round button. Either way, announce the number in the button’s aria-label.
If the badge is already rendered (.mtx-badge__badge), the component reuses it and only computes visibility and the maximum value from data-content.
With ES modules: Increment Reset to 0 Toggle invisible

Anchored to a child, the badge has aria-hidden="true": include the information in the control’s accessible name, for example aria-label="Notifications, 17 new" on the button. In data-standalone mode the number is read as text; use data-label to give it context (“4 unread”). Mark decorative icons with aria-hidden="true". Don’t convey information through the badge color alone: the aria-label text or the context must state its meaning. Badge isn’t interactive and doesn’t receive focus; if the wrapped element is a button, that button handles focus and keyboard.

d: A compact element that represents a tag, a filter, an input or an action; it can have an icon, an avatar and a delete button.

s.x: Chip represents a compact piece of information: a tag, an active filter, a recipient or a short action. Use it for tag lists, selectable filters or inputs the user can remove. For a primary action use Button; for a counter on an icon use Badge.
An empty element with data-mtx="chip" and data-label. The component generates the label, the icon and the delete button based on the attributes.
filled (default) uses a solid background; outlined uses a border and a transparent background.
medium (32px, default) and small (24px).
data-icon adds a Material Icons start icon. For an avatar, place a child with the mtx-chip__avatar class (it can be a 24px Avatar). A
data-color accepts the whole palette. In outlined, the color is applied to the text and the border.
data-clickable makes the chip interactive: pointer cursor, hover state, focus ring, role="button" and activation with Enter or Space. It emits mtx:chip:click.

data-deletable adds the delete button and emits mtx:chip:delete when it’s clicked or when Delete/Backspace is pressed while the chip has focus. The chip doesn’t remove itself: you decide what to do when you receive the event.
data-disabled disables the chip: it lowers the opacity, removes focus and blocks events.
Search filters: clickable chips that toggle between outlined (inactive) and filled primary (active), with aria-pressed to indicate their state.
If the structure already exists, the component reuses.mtx-chip__label,.mtx-chip__icon and.mtx-chip__delete.

Static chips are text with no role. Chips with data-clickable or data-deletable get role="button" and tabindex="0" (unless the element is already a <button> or <a>). As in MUI, the delete icon is not a nested control: it is a <span aria-hidden="true"> that is never focusable, so the role="button" chip contains no interactive descendants (axe nested-interactive). The chip is deleted with the mouse on the icon or with Delete/Backspace while the chip has focus; the chip announces those keys with aria-keyshortcuts="Delete Backspace". A pre-rendered <button class="mtx-chip__delete"> is converted into that <span>. The icon’s title comes from the i18n dictionary ( Delete in English, Eliminar in Spanish, following the element’s lang); make it specific with data-delete-label (for example, “Remove React”). For filters, indicate the active state with aria-pressed. Icons generated with data-icon have aria-hidden="true". Key Action Tab / Shift+Tab Moves focus between interactive chips. Enter / Space Activates a clickable chip (emits mtx:chip:click). Delete / Backspace On a deletable chip, emits mtx:chip:delete. Escape Removes focus from the chip.

d: A thin line that separates and groups content in lists, menus and layouts, horizontally or vertically and optionally with text.

s.x: Divider is a 1px line in the theme’s divider color that separates groups of content. Use it between sections of a list, between blocks of a form or between actions in a toolbar. Don’t use it as decoration everywhere: white space often separates better; and if you need a bordered container, use an outlined Paper.
An <hr> with data-mtx="divider". Being an <hr>, it already has the semantic separator role. Content of the first section. Content of the second section.

data-variant adjusts the side margins: with no value it spans the full width; middle leaves 16px on each side; inset leaves 72px on the left to align with the text of a list with icons or avatars. Full width Middle Inset

data-orientation="vertical" creates a vertical line that stretches to the height of its flex container. Use a <div>: the component adds role="separator" and aria-orientation="vertical" for you. data-flex-item makes a divider work as a flex item in containers that don’t stretch their children.
Write the text as the content of a <div> or use data-text. data-text-align places it on the left or the right (centered by default). CENTER

Inside a list, use an <li> as the divider to keep the HTML valid; inset aligns the line with the item text. The component does not give that <li> role="separator" (a list may only contain list items, axe rule list): an empty one is marked aria-hidden="true" as decorative, so screen readers don’t count it as an item. Alternatively, data-divider on each list-item draws a bottom border. Inbox Drafts Sent
An “or” separator between a social sign-in and the classic sign-in form. Continue with Google or
The classes work without JavaScript; the component only adds them based on the data-* attributes and generates the text <span>.
Divider has no methods or events of its own; you only need to initialize it if you create it dynamically. With ES modules:

<hr> has the implicit separator role; it’s the recommended option for horizontal dividers. On a <div> (or an <li> outside a list), the component adds role="separator" (unless you set your own role), and aria-orientation="vertical" on vertical dividers, as MUI does. Markup without JavaScript (pure CSS classes) must add them by hand. An <li> divider that is a direct child of <ul>, <ol> or role="list" keeps its list item role; if it’s empty it gets aria-hidden="true" (decorative), and with text it stays readable. A purely decorative divider inside a toolbar can have aria-hidden="true", or role="presentation" so the component doesn’t add separator. The text of a divider with text is readable content: write it meaningfully (“or”, “Section 2”), not with symbols.

d: Continuous vertical list of text, icons or avatars, with static or interactive items, subheaders, density and selection.

s.x: List groups related items in a continuous column: navigation menus, inboxes, settings or results. Each row can carry an icon or avatar, primary and secondary text, and a trailing action. For data with several comparable columns use Table; for a floating menu use Menu. The family registers these data-mtx values: list, list-item (static row), list-item-button (interactive row), list-item-text, list-item-icon, list-item-avatar, list-item-secondary-action and list-subheader. Each one adds its own mtx-* class, so the attribute is enough.
A <ul data-mtx="list"> with data-mtx="list-item" rows. data-icon adds a leading icon and data-secondary a secondary text; the component builds the inner structure. Inbox Drafts Sent

A row can have text only, an icon, an avatar, and primary plus secondary text. For an avatar use data-avatar="url" or write the data-mtx="avatar" inside the row: the component wraps it in mtx-list-item-avatar (56px wide, like MUI’s ListItemAvatar). Loose row text moves into mtx-list-item-text; controls, buttons and other components stay where they are. data-mtx="list-item-button" on a <button> (or an <a> for navigation) adds hover, visible focus, ripple and selection. Clicking a row marks it as selected ( mtx-list-item--selected) and unselects the previous one in the same list; it also emits the mtx:list:select event. Profile Preferences Security data-selectable="false" on the list (or data-no-select on a row) turns off automatic selection for rows that only run an action. Download Share

list-subheader titles groups of rows. It carries the mtx-list-subheader class; data-inset aligns the title with the text of rows that have an icon, and data-sticky pins it while scrolling inside the list. General Account Privacy Language Communications Notifications Email SMS
data-dense on the list reduces the vertical padding of all its rows (from 8px to 4px). Documents Photos Videos
A list with data-nested inside an item indents its rows by 48px. Selection is shared with the root list. Inbox Starred Invoices Sent

Wrap the action in mtx-list-item-secondary-action (or data-mtx="list-item-secondary-action"), the equivalent of MUI’s ListItemSecondaryAction: it sits at the end of the row, accepts several actions of any width, and a trailing IconButton snaps to the edge like edge="end". With the simplified syntax, data-icon and data-secondary build the icon and text without touching the action. Annual report.pdf MacBook Pro Sign out For a clickable row with an independent action (without nesting buttons), use a list-item with data-disable-padding that holds the list-item-button and the action as siblings. Side navigation with links: on an <a>, the selected row gets aria-current="page". Links are not underlined and inherit the list color; inside a Drawer, Paper, Card, Dialog or Menu the list is transparent so the surface shows through. Overview Orders Customers Reports Sales

Use <ul> / <li> so screen readers announce the number of items, and give the list a name with aria-label when it has no visible title. To separate items use data-divider on the items or an <li data-mtx="divider"> (see Divider): it stays a list item and, when empty, is hidden with aria-hidden. Never put an <hr> or an element with role="separator" directly inside <ul> / <ol> (axe rule list). Interactive rows must be a <button> (actions) or an <a href> (navigation) inside an <li>: that way they are focusable and activate from the keyboard with no extra code. Selection is conveyed with valid ARIA for each element: an <a> gets aria-current="page"; a <button>, aria-current="true"; only rows with role="option" or role="tab" (or another selectable role) get aria-selected. It is kept in sync on click, with data-selected and with the selected setter. Icons generated with data-icon are decorative; the row text is the accessible name. Secondary action buttons need their own aria-label. Key Action Tab / Shift+Tab Moves focus between interactive rows and actions. Enter Activates the focused row ( <button> or <a>). Space Activates the focused row if it is a <button>.

d: Displays data sets in rows and columns on a semantic HTML table, with density, sticky header, sorting, selection and pagination.

s.x: Table styles a regular HTML <table> with the MUI look and adds optional interactive pieces: row selection ( data-selectable), a toolbar ( table-toolbar), sort labels ( table-sort-label) and pagination ( table-pagination). Styles apply by descendant selectors and a MutationObserver also decorates rows added after initialization. Use it for multi-column data that users compare or scan. For a single column of items use List; for summary cards use Card.

Write a standard HTML table with data-mtx="table": the component adds the classes to thead, tbody, tfoot, rows and cells, and sets scope="col" on the header cells. Wrap it in data-mtx="table-container" so it scrolls horizontally inside its box on narrow screens. data-selectable on the table enables built-in selection (MUI’s EnhancedTable pattern): a checkbox column is added, the header checkbox selects or deselects every enabled row and becomes indeterminate on partial selection, and selected rows get mtx-table-row--selected. Each row is identified by data-id (an internal key is generated when missing) and the selection survives re-rendering the rows. With data-select-on-click, clicking anywhere on the row that is not a control also toggles it. The table emits mtx:table:selection-change with { selected, rows, count, reason }. data-mtx="table-toolbar" is the bar above the table (MUI’s EnhancedTableToolbar). With data-table="#id" it follows the selection: with no selected rows it shows the title ( data-title) and the data-show="default" children; with a selection it is highlighted ( mtx-table-toolbar--highlight, primary at 12%), replaces the title with the “N selected” counter (an aria-live="polite" region) and shows the data-show="selected" children. It has role="toolbar" and takes its name from the title. data-mtx="table-pagination" builds the rows-per-page selector, the visible range and the navigation buttons. With data-table="#selector" it paginates the rows of the given <tbody> on its own; without it, it works with data-count and you load the data when you receive mtx:table:page-change. A complete “data table”: Paper + toolbar + selectable table with sorting + pagination. With server-side pagination, remove data-table from the pagination, use data-count and render the page when you receive mtx:table:page-change: the selection by data-id is kept across pages (the header checkbox reflects only the visible rows).

Two mechanisms, usable with the simplified syntax or as plain classes: Variant per breakpoint (mobile-first, same breakpoints as Grid: sm 600px, md 900px, lg 1200px, xl 1536px): data-variant-{sm|md|lg|xl}="h3" or the mtx-typography--{bp}-{variant} class. The base variant applies on mobile and each breakpoint replaces it from there up. Fluid scale (equivalent to MUI’s responsiveFontSizes): data-responsive or the mtx-typography--responsive class. h1–h6 scale with clamp() between their mobile size (≤600px) and their desktop size (≥1200px): h1 3.5→6rem, h2 2.375→3.75rem, h3 2→3rem, h4 1.5625→2.125rem, h5 1.25→1.5rem, h6 1.125→1.25rem. The surface has role="tooltip" and is linked to the trigger following the WAI-ARIA tooltip pattern: If the trigger has no accessible name (an icon-only button without aria-label / aria-labelledby /text), the text is applied as its aria-label as soon as the page loads (and for content added later). This is the case for MUI’s Tooltip by default. If it already has a name, the name is kept and the tooltip is linked with aria-describedby while it is visible. If both texts are identical it is not duplicated. It appears on keyboard focus (:focus-visible heuristic: Tab yes, mouse click no) and hides on blur. Hoverable (WCAG 1.4.13): the pointer can move from the trigger onto the tooltip without it disappearing (an invisible bridge covers the gap). Dismissible: Escape hides it without moving focus. Do not put interactive content in a tooltip; use a Popover. It respects prefers-reduced-motion (no scale animation) and draws a border in forced-colors mode. Key Action Tab Focusing a trigger shows its tooltip after the delay. Escape Hides the visible tooltip, and only it: an open menu, popover or dialog underneath stays open until the next Escape.

d: Circular and linear indicators that show an operation is in progress or how much is left before it finishes.

s.x: Progress brings together MUI’s two indicators: CircularProgress ( data-mtx="circular-progress") and LinearProgress ( data-mtx="linear-progress"). Use them to show that something is loading or being processed: indeterminate when you don’t know how long it will take, determinate when you know the percentage. Don’t use them for static metrics that never advance (a chart or plain text is clearer), or to block the whole screen without explanation (pair them with a text or use a Dialog).

A single element is enough: the component generates the SVG or the bars, role="progressbar" and the accessible name. Without data-value the indicator is indeterminate; with data-value (0–100) it becomes determinate.

indeterminate spins while the stroke grows and shrinks (MUI’s animation); determinate draws an arc proportional to the value, starting at the top. data-disable-shrink keeps the stroke length fixed and only rotates, which helps when the main thread is busy. data-track adds the background ring.

Four variants, as in MUI: indeterminate, determinate, buffer (inferred from data-value-buffer: shows the value, the preloaded part and an animated dotted pattern) and query (indeterminate in reverse, for the phase before loading starts). The bar is 4px tall; data-rounded rounds its ends.

data-size sets the diameter in px (40 by default) and data-thickness the stroke width inside the 44-unit viewBox (3.6 by default). For the linear bar, change the --mtx-linear-progress-height variable.

data-show-label displays the rounded percentage: centered inside the circle (MUI’s “CircularProgress with label” pattern) or to the right of the bar (“LinearProgress with label”). The number is decorative ( aria-hidden); screen readers read the value from aria-valuenow.

data-color accepts primary (default), secondary, error, warning, info, success and inherit (uses the container’s text color). The linear track is the same color lightened by 62% in the light theme and darkened by 50% in the dark theme, as in MUI.

data-min and data-max (0 and 100 by default) let you express the value in your own units: aria-valuenow and aria-valuemax reflect those units and the component computes the percentage to draw. Team seats · 7 of 10

Loading a region: mark the container being updated with aria-busy="true" and remove it when done, so screen readers wait for the final content. Loading button: insert a decorative indicator with Materix.createCircularProgress({ size: 20, color: 'inherit', decorative: true }), set aria-busy="true" and disabled on the button and change its text. Reduced motion: with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the circle spins more slowly without shrinking the stroke, indeterminate bars slow down and the buffer pattern stops. Loading comments…

The root gets role="progressbar" and an accessible name: data-label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; if none is present, i18n progress.loading (“Loading” / “Cargando” depending on the document language or data-locale). aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax are only exposed for determinate and buffer; they are removed for indeterminate and query, as WAI-ARIA recommends. The SVG and the percentage label have aria-hidden="true", so the value is announced only once. Mark the region being loaded with aria-busy="true" and, if you want the result announced, with aria-live="polite". Inside a button or another control that already communicates loading ( aria-busy, “Saving…” text), use data-decorative or createCircularProgress({ decorative: true }) to avoid a duplicate announcement. Honors prefers-reduced-motion: slower rotation without shrinking, slower bars and a static buffer pattern. It is not interactive: it doesn’t receive focus or respond to the keyboard.

d: Content-shaped placeholders shown while data loads, with a pulse or wave animation.

s.x: Skeleton displays a grey block shaped like content that hasn’t arrived yet (text, avatar, image, card). It reduces perceived waiting and avoids layout shifts when the data appears. Use it for short loads of content with a known structure; if you don’t know what shape the result will have, or the operation doesn’t load content (saving, sending), use Progress.

A single element with data-mtx="skeleton". Without a variant it is a text line that fills the available width and the height of the typography. data-width and data-height accept numbers (px) or any CSS unit.
Four shapes, as in MUI: text (default; scaled to 60% of the line height so it keeps the vertical rhythm of text), circular, rectangular (no radius) and rounded (4px radius).

data-animation="pulse" (default, the opacity oscillates), "wave" (a highlight sweeps across the block) or "false" (static). With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is disabled automatically.

The text variant inherits the size of the typography around it: place it inside the same element that will hold the real text and it gets its exact height. Circular shapes follow the Avatar heights (24, 40 and 56px).
data-lines="3" generates several text lines inside the element; the last one is shorter (60% by default, configurable with data-last-width).

When the skeleton wraps content, it takes its exact size and hides it with visibility: hidden (like children in MUI). No need to repeat measurements: the Avatar, Button or heading itself becomes the mold. Save changes A real-length heading

To switch between placeholder and content without custom JavaScript, mark the container with data-loading and its direct children with data-skeleton-placeholder (visible while loading) and data-skeleton-content (visible once loaded). Materix.skeleton.set(container, bool) changes the state, syncs aria-busy and emits mtx:skeleton:change. d: Brief, temporary notification at an edge of the screen that confirms an action and can offer to undo it.

s.x: Snackbar shows a short floating message at an edge of the screen to confirm the outcome of an action (“Email sent”, “Item deleted”) and, optionally, offer a single action such as “Undo”. It does not interrupt the user and can close on its own. Do not use it for errors the user must resolve (use an Alert next to the content) or for mandatory decisions (use a Dialog).

Declare the snackbar with data-message anywhere in the <body>: it stays hidden until you call open(). There is no declarative open attribute, so the trigger needs one line of JavaScript. Show snackbar

data-action generates a.mtx-snackbar__action button to the right of the message. With data-close-on-action the snackbar closes when it is clicked ( reason: 'action'); every click also emits mtx:snackbar:action, which you can listen for to run your logic. Delete email

data-anchor supports six positions. On screens 600px wide or less, the snackbar stretches to the full width with an 8px margin on each side. top-left top-center top-right bottom-left bottom-center bottom-right

data-duration sets the auto-hide delay in milliseconds. If omitted (or set to none), the snackbar does not close on its own: only with Escape, a click away, the action or close(). The timer pauses while the pointer or focus is inside and restarts with the full duration when they leave. 2 seconds 8 seconds No auto-hide

The component does not manage a queue: two snackbars open at the same position overlap. To show them one at a time (MUI’s Consecutive Snackbars pattern), close the current one and open the next when mtx:snackbar:close is received.

For one-off confirmations you don’t need to declare a snackbar: Materix.snackbar.show(options) creates a shared snackbar in <body> the first time ( role="status", 4 s duration) and reuses it afterwards. d: Panels that show and hide related sections of content behind a clickable summary, ideal for FAQs and grouped settings.

s.x: Accordion organizes content into collapsible panels: a clickable summary (AccordionSummary) shows or hides the details (AccordionDetails) with a height transition. Use it for FAQs, sectioned settings or secondary information that shouldn’t take up space permanently. Don’t use it for primary navigation (use Tabs or a Drawer) or to hide content users always need to see.

A <div data-mtx="accordion"> with data-summary generates the <h3> heading, the button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, the expand_more icon and the collapsible region. The div’s content becomes the details. The summary is bold (weight 500) and, when expanded, gets its own background and a divider that separates it from the content (see Summary style). Adjacent panels are grouped visually: they share 1px separators and only the first and last ones get rounded corners. Adjacent panels share 1px separators, just like MUI. When expanded, the panel moves 16px away from its neighbors. This panel starts expanded with data-expanded.

Progressive enhancement: a <details data-mtx="accordion"> works without JavaScript. On initialization the native element is kept and gets the MUI styling, the height animation and the icon. The open attribute sets the initial state, and the browser’s find-in-page (Ctrl+F) opens the panel that contains the match. Does it work without JavaScript? Yes. The native element opens and closes on its own; Materix adds the look, the transition and keyboard support. Can the browser's search find the hidden text? Yes: collapsed panels open when Ctrl+F finds a match inside them. A <summary> can’t live inside a heading, so the details form doesn’t generate an <h3>. If the heading outline matters for your page, use the <div> form.

By default the accordion is a Paper surface with elevation 1. data-variant="outlined" uses a 1px border (adjacent borders are merged), data-elevation="0" makes it flat and data-square removes the rounded corners. By default the summary uses medium weight (500) and, while the panel is expanded, an --mtx-color-action-selected background plus a bottom divider, so the heading stands apart from the content in both light and dark themes. Focus ( --mtx-color-action-focus) takes precedence over that background, and a disabled panel keeps its reduced opacity. data-summary-style="plain" (on the panel or on the group) restores MUI’s flat look: regular weight, no background and no divider. Tune it with the --mtx-accordion-summary-* CSS variables. Deliberate deviation from MUI MUI’s AccordionSummary uses regular weight and the same background as the details. Materix emphasizes the summary by default so an open panel’s heading is easy to tell from its content. Use data-summary-style="plain" for the original MUI look. data-mtx="accordion-group" keeps a single panel open (MUI’s “Controlled accordion” pattern) and enables arrow, Home and End navigation between summaries. With data-exclusive="false" several panels can be open. The group propagates data-variant, data-square, data-elevation and data-disable-gutters to panels that don’t declare them. d: Top bar with the title, navigation and primary actions of the current screen.

s.x: App Bar is the application’s top bar: it displays the screen title, the navigation button and the most frequent actions inside a Toolbar. Use it once per screen as a header. To switch between views at the same level use Tabs, for primary navigation combine it with a Drawer, and for a floating primary action use a Fab.

A <header data-mtx="app-bar"> with data-title, data-start-icon and data-end-icon generates the.mtx-toolbar, the title and the IconButtons. Any children you write are placed after the title. The bar is fixed by default; these demos use data-position="static" so it stays inside the page. Login

data-color accepts primary, secondary, default (paper surface; the value used when none is set), transparent and inherit. data-elevation changes the shadow (4 by default). With data-elevation="0" the bar gets mtx-app-bar--flat and, in default, a single bottom divider instead of the shadow. transparent never has a shadow. Colors derive from the bar’s contrast color, so they stay correct in the dark theme (where primary is light with dark text).

The regular Toolbar is 56 px tall on mobile and 64 px from 600 px up, with 16 and 24 px side gutters. data-dense reduces it to 48 px. The prominent variant (128 px) is only available with the BEM syntax (.mtx-toolbar--prominent).

data-start-icon adds the navigation button (.mtx-toolbar__navigation-icon) and data-end-icon a trailing action. Set their accessible names with data-start-icon-label and data-end-icon-label; without them, the menu icon (or any start icon with data-drawer) is labeled “Open navigation” from the i18n dictionary and other icons fall back to their name. With data-drawer="id" the navigation button toggles that Drawer. For multiple actions write the buttons yourself as children (mark the title with.mtx-toolbar__title). Photos

Inside the Toolbar, text and outlined Buttons and Icon Buttons inherit the bar color (like color="inherit" in MUI), so they read well on primary, secondary and default without extra classes. contained buttons keep their background/contrast pair: pick a color that stands out on the bar (e.g. data-color="secondary" on a primary bar). Disabled buttons keep their state color. Docs Login Get started

d: A surface that groups content and actions about a single subject: header, image, text and buttons.

s.x: Card groups the information and actions of a single item on an elevated surface: a product, a recipe, a profile. It’s built from optional parts —header, media, content, actions and action area— generated from data-* attributes. Use it when the block is self-contained and scannable within a collection; for a generic surface without structure use Paper, and for dense lists use List.

data-title, data-subheader, data-avatar and data-image generate the header and the image; the content and actions are declared with data-mtx="card-content" and data-mtx="card-actions". A Mediterranean dish with bomba rice, saffron, free-range chicken and fresh vegetables.

By default the card has elevation 1. data-variant="outlined" delimits it with a border and no shadow; data-raised raises it to 8 (like MUI’s raised); data-elevation accepts 0–8, 12, 16 and 24; data-square removes the radius. Default Elevation 1. Outlined Border, no shadow. Raised Elevation 8. Square Elevation 4, no radius.

The header (.mtx-card__header) is generated if there’s a data-title, data-subheader or data-avatar. The avatar is a primary Avatar with the given text; data-action-icon adds an IconButton on the right with the given Material Icons icon. Title only. Avatar, title, subheader and action.

By default it’s placed after the header; data-media-top puts it at the top and data-media-height (or data-height) sets the height in pixels. An image generated this way is decorative: if it conveys information, use your own data-mtx="card-media" with data-alt. More than 6,000 species, found on every continent except Antarctica. Use <article> or <section> as the root when the card is self-contained content. On a data-clickable card without a <button> / <a>, role="button" and tabindex="0" are added; its accessible name comes from its content (title, subheader and text). Avoid an aria-label that does not contain the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name, axe label-content-name-mismatch); if you need one, start it with the visible title. Prefer CardActionArea on a native <button> or <a>: it keeps its semantics and leaves the card-actions buttons as independent controls (don’t nest buttons inside the area). Images generated with data-image on the card are decorative ( aria-hidden) unless you add data-image-alt; use it when the image conveys information. IconButtons in the actions need an aria-label. Key Action Tab Moves through the action area, the clickable card and the buttons. Enter / Space Activates the focused clickable card or action area.

d: The base Material Design surface, with background, border radius and shadow, that groups content and expresses elevation.

s.x: Paper is the physical surface of Material Design: a container with a paper background, a 4px border radius and a shadow that conveys its elevation. It is the visual foundation of Card, Dialog, Menu and AppBar. Use it to group arbitrary content on top of the page background; if the block has a header, an image and actions, use a Card directly.
A <div data-mtx="paper"> gets the.mtx-paper class with elevation 1. Change the shadow with data-elevation. Elevation 1 (default) Elevation 8

The default variant sets the surface apart with a shadow. data-variant="outlined" outlines it with a 1px border ( --mtx-color-divider) and no shadow; data-elevation="0" makes it flat. Shadow Border Flat

Only MUI elevations 0 to 8, 12, 16 and 24 exist as tokens ( --mtx-elevation-*). Any other data-elevation value generates an unstyled class and the surface keeps elevation 1. 0 1 2 3 4 6 8 12 16 24 Typical use (MUI) Elevation Card at rest, base Paper 1 Raised Card ( raised), Menu 8 AppBar 4 Drawer 16 Dialog 24
Corners use --mtx-shape-radius (4px). data-square makes them straight, which is useful for surfaces flush with the edges of the viewport. Rounded Square Outlined square

Paper consumes --mtx-color-background-paper and --mtx-color-text-primary, so it follows the theme without touching the component. The data-mtx-theme="dark" attribute also works on a specific container. In the dark theme, as in MUI, each elevation adds a white overlay ( --mtx-overlay-elevation-N, alpha = (4.5·ln(N+1) + 2) / 100) through background-image, so higher surfaces look lighter even though the shadow is barely visible. outlined has no overlay. Elevation 0 Elevation 1 Elevation 4 Elevation 8 Elevation 24 Outlined
Paper is the usual container for Grid items: the column sets the width and Paper provides the surface. Sales $12,480 Orders 326 Returns 4
The classes can be written directly (SSR or templates); the component does not duplicate the ones that already exist.

Paper has no methods or events of its own: it only translates its data-* attributes into classes on initialization (once). To change the elevation afterwards, toggle the mtx-paper--elevation-* classes.

The elevation classes are declared after --outlined in the stylesheet: if you combine data-variant="outlined" with data-elevation, the shadow comes back. Use one or the other.

Paper is purely visual and adds no roles or ARIA: use the appropriate semantic element ( <section>, <article>, <aside>) and give it a heading if it groups relevant content. Elevation does not convey information on its own; in the dark theme the white overlay helps, but use outlined or a heading when the surface must be clearly delimited. It is not interactive: if the whole surface must be clickable, use a Card with data-clickable or a CardActionArea.

d: Floating Paper with arbitrary content anchored to a trigger. Closes on click away or Escape and returns focus to the trigger.

s.x: A Popover displays any content (text, forms, cards) on a floating Paper surface anchored to another element, like MUI’s Popover. Use it for filters, quick details, small confirmations or an account card. For a list of actions use a Menu; for a short text label, a Tooltip; for a task that blocks the page, a Dialog.

An element with data-mtx="popover" and an id, and a trigger with data-open-popover="#id". It opens below the trigger aligned to its start edge, with elevation 8. Focus moves to the first control (or to the panel) and returns to the trigger when it closes. Open popover The content of the popover. The panel is ported to <body> when it opens, so ancestors with overflow: hidden or their own z-index never clip it. Content padding is up to you: use utilities such as mtx-p-2.

data-placement uses the same engine as Tooltip ( top|bottom|left|right with -start|-end; default bottom-start), with automatic flipping and shifting. data-offset sets the gap in px (0 by default, as in MUI). top bottom-end right · offset 8 Above, centered. Below, aligned to the end. To the right.

MUI’s API: data-anchor-origin="vertical horizontal" is the point on the anchor and data-transform-origin the point on the popover attached to it. Values are top|center|bottom and left|center|right, or pixels. The popover stays 16 px from the viewport edges (MUI’s marginThreshold) and the grow animation starts from the transform origin. bottom left → top left center center → center center top right → bottom right anchor: bottom left · transform: top left anchor: center center · transform: center center anchor: top right · transform: bottom right When either origin attribute is present it takes precedence over data-placement.

Any button can be the trigger. Icon-only ones need an accessible name: aria-label or a data-mtx-tooltip, which provides it. The trigger gets aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-controls and a synchronized aria-expanded. Details Order #48213 Shipped on October 12, estimated delivery in 48 h. The heading inside the popover becomes its name automatically ( aria-labelledby).

A disabled trigger does not open the popover. Buttons with data-mtx-popover-close inside the popover close it (and return focus). Disabled Archive project Archive the project? You can restore it for 30 days. Cancel Archive

By default the popover is non-modal: it does not trap focus or lock scrolling, and tabbing out of it closes it. With data-modal it behaves like MUI’s Popover (which is built on Modal): it traps Tab, locks page scrolling and sets aria-modal="true". data-autofocus on a control chooses the initial focus. Rename Rename Cancel Save
open({ x, y }) anchors the popover to a viewport point instead of an element (MUI’s anchorPosition), for example the cursor position in a contextmenu event.
An account card opened from the avatar in an app bar, aligned to the end: LG Laura Gómez's account LG Laura Gómez laura@example.com Sign out Table filters: Filters Filter orders Apply

A button inside the popover can open a Dialog. Both surfaces share the layer stack: interacting with the dialog is not a “click outside” for the popover, the first Escape closes only the dialog (focus returns to the button inside the popover) and the second one closes the popover. Options Advanced… Close

After initialization the popover has this structure. You can write it as is for SSR: the component keeps an existing role, aria-label / aria-labelledby and tabindex. A trigger can also be declared with aria-controls.
With ES modules: open(this) toggle(this) Opened from code. close()

Materix.computePosition(anchor, floating, options) and Materix.autoUpdate(anchor, floating, update) are public, for your own floating surfaces: The result also includes side, align (physical, after flipping and RTL) and arrowOffset (center of the anchor relative to the surface). The anchor can be virtual: any object with getBoundingClientRect().

The popover has role="dialog". Its name comes from data-label ( aria-label), from data-popover-title or from the first internal heading ( aria-labelledby). With data-modal it also gets aria-modal="true". The trigger gets aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-controls and an aria-expanded synchronized with the state. When it opens, focus moves to [data-autofocus], to the first focusable control or to the panel itself ( tabindex="-1"). When it closes with Escape, the trigger or a close button, focus returns to the element that had it. When it opens from a trigger, the trigger is stored as the focus return target even if the browser does not focus it on click (WebKit/Safari), so Escape and close actions always return focus to it. Clicking outside closes it without stealing focus from the element that was clicked; if the click lands on a non-focusable area and focus would be lost, it returns to the trigger. If the trigger only shows an avatar or initials, name it with visually hidden text ( …) instead of an aria-label that does not contain the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). d: Hierarchical navigation trail that shows where the user is and lets them jump back to any parent level.

s.x: Breadcrumbs renders the path from the root of the site or app to the current page, like MUI’s Breadcrumbs: a <nav> with an ordered list, separators hidden from assistive technologies and the last item marked with aria-current="page". Use it in hierarchies of three or more levels (catalogs, documentation, file managers). Do not use it as primary navigation or for linear flows: use a Drawer or Tabs for sections, and a stepper for steps.

A single <ol data-mtx="breadcrumbs">. The component wraps it in <nav aria-label="breadcrumb">, turns each <a> into a Materix Link ( color="inherit", underline on hover), inserts the separators and marks the last item as the current page. Home Catalog Accessories If the last item must stay a link (for example to reload the page), add aria-current="page" yourself: the component respects it and does not mark any other item. Home Catalog Headphones

data-separator accepts any text (default /) or the name of a Material icon: a value made of lowercase letters, digits and underscores, with three or more characters ( navigate_next, chevron_right), is rendered as an icon. Home Catalog Accessories Home Catalog Accessories Home Catalog Accessories

data-icon on the link (or on the text <span>) adds a decorative Material icon before the label. As in MUI, the hover underline and the focus ring keep the icon aligned: only the label is underlined. Home Projects Website redesign

When there are more items than data-max-items (8 by default), only data-items-before-collapse (1) and data-items-after-collapse (1) are shown, separated by a “Show path” button. Activating it reveals the hidden items and moves focus to the first one. Home Catalog Accessories New collection Belts Home Documents 2026 Accounting Q3 Invoices

Like MUI, it uses body1 in text.secondary and the current page in text.primary. For a more compact trail, add a Typography class ( mtx-typography--body2) to the element. Settings Security Settings Security

Links show the Link states (underline on hover, focus ring with Tab). A trail link can be disabled with data-disabled, and data-color on the <a> changes its color. Home Archived Order #4821 Home Customers Ana Torres

It can also be initialized on a <nav> whose direct children are the links: the component creates the <ol> and one <li> per child. On a <div> it adds role="navigation". Help Billing Change payment method
Page header of an admin panel: trail, title and main action. Dashboard Users Edit profile Edit profile Save changes
Pre-rendered structure (SSR). It already looks right without JavaScript; with data-mtx the component reuses the nodes and repaints the separators without duplicating them.

setItems() rebuilds the whole trail, which is ideal for SPAs and folder navigation. Items without href that are not the current page are rendered as a Link on a <button>; data is copied to data-* attributes and comes back in the event. The mtx:breadcrumbs:navigate event is cancelable: call preventDefault() to handle navigation yourself. My Drive Open subfolder With ES modules: Materix.getInstance() returns the same instance for the original <ol> and for the <nav> it is wrapped in; instance.element is always the <nav>.

Attribute Values Default Description data-mtx breadcrumbs — Initializes the component on an <ol> / <ul> (wrapped in <nav>), a <nav> with an <ol>, or a <nav> / <div> with direct links. data-separator text or icon name / Separator between items. Lowercase names with _ and 3+ characters render as a Material icon. data-max-items integer 8 Maximum number of visible items before collapsing. 0 disables collapsing. data-items-before-collapse integer 1 Items shown before the collapse button. data-items-after-collapse integer 1 Items shown after the collapse button. data-expand-label text i18n breadcrumbs.showPath Accessible label of the collapse button. data-icon (on <a>, <span> or <li>) icon name — Decorative icon before the label. data-color, data-underline, data-disabled (on <a>) see Link inherit, hover Link options for each item.

Class Description mtx-breadcrumbs Root <nav>: body1 typography (zero specificity, so mtx-typography--* can override it) in text.secondary. mtx-breadcrumbs--collapsed Added while there are hidden items. mtx-breadcrumbs__ol Flex list with wrapping, no bullets or margins. mtx-breadcrumbs__li Item. mtx-breadcrumbs__link Item link (a Materix Link). mtx-breadcrumbs__text Item without a link (usually the current page). mtx-breadcrumbs__item--with-icon Link or text with an icon: reserves 24px + 4px for the icon and keeps the hover underline under the text only. mtx-breadcrumbs__icon Decorative 24px icon ( aria-hidden), vertically centered and outside the text flow, so it is never underlined. mtx-breadcrumbs__separator Separator <li> with aria-hidden="true" and 8px horizontal margin. mtx-breadcrumbs__collapsed <li> holding the collapse button. mtx-breadcrumbs__collapse-button “Show path” button (MoreHoriz icon 24×16).

Method Returns Description setItems(items) void Replaces the trail. items: [{ label, href?, icon?, current?, data? }]. Without current, the last item is the current page. Throws TypeError if it is not an array. getItems() Array Copy of the items: { label, href, icon, current, data }. expand(focus?) void Shows all items; with focus = true it moves focus to the first revealed item. collapse() void Re-applies collapsing. expanded (getter) boolean Whether the trail was expanded. maxItems (getter/setter) number Maximum number of visible items. destroy() void Removes listeners. Unlinks the instance: getInstance() then returns undefined.

Event detail Emitted when mtx:breadcrumbs:navigate { index, href, label, current, item, originalEvent } A trail link or button is activated. Cancelable: preventDefault() cancels the native navigation. mtx:breadcrumbs:expand — The collapsed items are revealed.

Variable Usage --mtx-breadcrumbs-separator-gap Horizontal margin of the separator (8px). --mtx-breadcrumbs-collapse-bg, --mtx-breadcrumbs-collapse-bg-hover, --mtx-breadcrumbs-collapse-color Collapse button colors (grey 100/200/700, inverted in dark theme). --mtx-type-body1, --mtx-color-text-secondary, --mtx-color-text-primary Typography and colors of the trail and the current page. --mtx-focus-ring-width, --mtx-focus-ring-color Focus ring of the collapse button.

Landmark <nav> with aria-label="breadcrumb" (translated through i18n breadcrumbs.label; your own aria-label or aria-labelledby is kept). On a <div>, role="navigation" is added. Ordered list ( <ol>): screen readers announce the number of levels. Separators are <li aria-hidden="true">, so they are not read. The current page has aria-current="page". The collapse button is a real <button> with the translated label “Show path”; after expanding, focus moves to the first revealed item so it is not lost. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves through the trail links and the collapse button. Enter Follows the link or expands the trail. Space Expands the trail (collapse button) or activates an item rendered as a button.

d: Side panel for navigation or supplementary content: temporary, persistent, permanent or responsive, with a generated header and footer and an app shell pattern.

s.x: Drawer is a panel that slides in from an edge of the screen to show the app’s navigation or supplementary content (filters, details, options), like MUI’s Drawer. Use it for primary navigation on mobile (temporary) or as a fixed sidebar on desktop (permanent). For a decision or a short form that interrupts the flow use a Dialog; for a short list of actions on an item, a Menu.

A data-mtx="drawer" container with its content directly inside. data-title generates the header with a title and a close button; the content is wrapped in a scrollable panel and a backdrop is created. Any element with data-mtx-drawer-open="id" opens it. Open navigation Inbox Starred Sent Drafts It closes with Escape, a click on the backdrop or outside the panel, the X, or any inner element that has data-mtx-drawer-close. Clicking a list item selects it (the others are deselected within the drawer).

The main recipe for an application, with no CSS of your own — the same structure as MUI’s Responsive drawer + Clipped under the app bar: A fixed App Bar. Its generated navigation icon becomes the drawer trigger with data-drawer="id". A flex row ( mtx-d-flex) with the drawer in data-variant="responsive" + data-clipped: temporary (modal, above the App Bar) below data-breakpoint and permanent (a fixed-width box in the flow, sticky right below the App Bar) from it upwards. Same markup, no duplicated navigation. A <main class="mtx-flex-1 mtx-min-w-0"> that starts with.mtx-toolbar-offset (a spacer as tall as the App Bar: 56px on mobile, 64px from 600px). The menu icon is hidden automatically while the drawer is permanent ( mtx-drawer-trigger--hidden) and gets aria-controls / aria-expanded. data-mtx-drawer-close on the links closes the drawer after navigating on mobile; it does nothing while it’s permanent. data-header="temporary" shows the generated header (title + close button) only in temporary mode, because on desktop the App Bar already shows the brand..mtx-drawer__content is a flex column: a child with mtx-mt-auto stays pinned to the bottom (upgrade card, version, sign-out…). data-variant chooses the behavior, just like MUI: temporary (default): modal over the page with a backdrop; it locks <body> scrolling, traps focus and returns it on close. persistent: opens and closes without a backdrop; the page stays interactive. permanent: always visible and impossible to close. As in MUI, it’s a fixed-width box in the flow of a flex row ( flex-shrink: 0) whose panel is sticky and as tall as the viewport ( 100dvh), so it doesn’t scroll with the page. responsive: temporary below data-breakpoint ( sm 600px, md 900px by default, lg 1200px, xl 1536px) and permanent from it upwards, with the same markup (see “App shell”). With data-absolute, the drawer (and its backdrop) are positioned inside the parent container instead of the window, useful for embedded panels like these; a contained permanent drawer takes the container’s height instead of the viewport’s. temporary persistent (toggle) Inbox Sent Inbox Sent Overview Orders Customers Page content next to the permanent drawer.

data-anchor sets the edge: left (default), right, top or bottom. Top and bottom drawers span the full width and fit their content (equivalent to a bottom sheet). left right top bottom Main navigation. Details or filters panel. OK Global notice dropping down from the top. Email Copy link

Without data-width the width is responsive: min(85vw, 320px) below 600px, 280px from 600px and 300px from 900px. Side drawers never exceed 85% of the window, so part of the page always stays visible. data-width Width Variable — min(85vw, 320px) · 280px (≥ 600px) · 300px (≥ 900px) --mtx-drawer-width-mobile · --mtx-drawer-width-tablet · --mtx-drawer-width narrow 200px --mtx-drawer-width-narrow wide 360px --mtx-drawer-width-wide full (or full-width) 100vw — CSS length ( 450px, 40vw …) The given value written to width and --mtx-drawer-width narrow wide 450px Compact. For forms and filters. Arbitrary length.

data-title creates a header with a title ( h3) and a close button; data-close-button="false" omits the button (it’s never generated in permanent). data-user-name, data-user-email and data-user-avatar create a user header with an Avatar (the name’s initial by default). It takes precedence over data-title. data-footer-version and data-footer-action create a fixed footer with a text and an error -colored text button that closes the drawer; data-footer-action-icon changes its icon ( logout by default). data-padded="true" adds 20px of padding to the content, keeping the header and footer edge to edge. data-header="temporary" shows the generated header only while the drawer is temporary (useful in responsive). Any element can use the mtx-drawer__temporary-only / mtx-drawer__permanent-only classes for the same purpose. data-subtitle adds a subtitle stacked under the title ( mtx-drawer__heading). The header and footer stay fixed and only the middle section scrolls. Open account menu General Dashboard Messages Settings Preferences Help

Besides open and closed, you can limit the implicit ways a temporary drawer closes: data-disable-backdrop-click: neither the backdrop nor an outside click closes it. data-disable-escape: Escape doesn’t close it. data-backdrop="false" (or data-hide-backdrop): no backdrop; an outside click still closes it. Edit without saving Choose an option to close. Discard Save

Attribute Where Action data-mtx-drawer-open="id" Any element Opens the id drawer. data-mtx-drawer-toggle="id" Any element Toggles the id drawer (menu button). data-mtx-drawer-close="id" Any element Closes the id drawer (reason closeButtonClick). data-mtx-drawer-close (no value) Inside the drawer Closes the drawer that contains it. data-drawer-autofocus Inside the drawer Element that receives focus on open (otherwise, the first focusable one). The open and toggle triggers get aria-controls and an aria-expanded that stays in sync as the drawer opens and closes. In a responsive drawer they also get mtx-drawer-trigger--hidden ( display: none) while it is permanent. An App Bar with data-start-icon + data-drawer="id" generates this trigger for you.

In the clipped pattern the App Bar spans the full width and the drawer starts below it. data-clipped applies to permanent, responsive (in its permanent mode) and persistent: the drawer starts at --mtx-app-bar-height (56px on mobile, 64px from 600px) and stacks below the App Bar ( --mtx-z-index-app-bar − 1). The temporary drawer ignores clipped: it’s a modal ( --mtx-z-index-modal) and covers the App Bar, as in MUI. The full-page recipe is in “App shell”. Inside a container, you get the same effect with a contained permanent drawer in the row below the App Bar: My app Overview Orders Reports Main content

data-variant="responsive" replaces the old two-drawer pattern. The drawer watches (min-width: <breakpoint>) with matchMedia and, when crossing it: to permanent: releases the modal (backdrop, scroll lock, focus trap) if it was open, sets role="navigation" (unless you set your own role), removes role="dialog" / aria-modal from the panel and hides its triggers. to temporary: closes it, restores the panel’s role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" (named by the drawer’s aria-label or the header title), aria-hidden="true", shows the triggers and, if focus was inside the drawer, moves it to the trigger. Fires mtx:drawer:mode-change with { mode, previousMode }. The current mode is in drawer.mode. Without matchMedia (SSR, tests) it behaves as temporary.

An item with data-mtx-collapse-trigger="id" and aria-expanded expands an mtx-collapse container with a nested list ( data-nested, 48px indent). The mtx-collapse-indicator rotates 90° and data-no-select prevents the parent item from becoming selected. Open projects Overview My projects Website Mobile app
