temporary: the inner panel gets role="dialog" and aria-modal="true"; focus is trapped inside and returns to the trigger on close. The trap always intercepts Tab / Shift + Tab and moves focus explicitly through the tabbable elements, so links are included even in WebKit/Safari (which skips them with Tab by default). persistent gets role="region" and permanent gets role="navigation". The container keeps aria-hidden in sync. Give the content a name: a <nav aria-label="…"> for navigation, or an aria-label on the drawer. The generated close button’s aria-label comes from the i18n dictionary ( drawer.close: “Close” / “Cerrar”), resolved with the language of the drawer or the page. responsive: the ARIA semantics switch with the mode (see “Responsive drawer”) and focus is never left inside a hidden drawer. Declarative triggers get aria-controls and aria-expanded. Collapsed submenus ( mtx-collapse) get hidden and inert, and an expanded submenu inherits the visibility of the drawer: inside a closed drawer ( aria-hidden="true") none of its links are focusable (axe aria-hidden-focus). d: MUI-styled text link on a native <a>: palette colors and three underline modes, without losing semantics.

s.x: Link applies the MUI link style (palette color and an always-visible underline, the MUI v5 default; it inherits the surrounding typography, like variant="inherit") to a native <a href>, so it keeps the browser’s navigation, focus and context menu. Use it to navigate to another page or section from within text. If the action does not navigate (save, open a dialog, submit a form), use a Button with the text variant; for primary app destinations, use a Drawer or Tabs.
A single <a> element with data-mtx="link". The component adds the mtx-link class and, if present, the data-color and data-underline modifiers. View documentation

data-color accepts the six palette colors, text-primary, text-secondary and inherit. Without the attribute, the link uses primary. primary secondary error warning info success text-primary text-secondary inherit takes the color of the surrounding text, which is useful inside alerts, app bars or colored surfaces. Your subscription expires tomorrow. Renew now Contrast On a white background, warning (#ed6c02) and info (#0288d1) fall below 4.5:1 for 14px text. Use them for secondary links or next to text that already explains the destination, and prefer primary for links inside paragraphs.

data-underline controls the decoration: always (default, as in MUI v5: a soft underline at 40% of the link color that becomes solid on hover; required inside paragraphs), hover (only on hover) and none (never, not even on hover). Use hover or none only for links that are not inside running text (navigation, lists, footers). Behavior change Before this version the default was hover. To keep the previous look on a specific link, add data-underline="hover" (or the mtx-link--underline-hover class). Links that Breadcrumbs renders keep the hover underline. always (default) hover none

In running text, color must not be the only cue: keep the default underline ( always) so the link can also be told apart without perceiving color. By creating an account you agree to the terms of service and the privacy policy. You can change your preferences at any time from the settings panel. Link typography mtx-link inherits the surrounding typography (family, size, weight and line height), like variant="inherit" in MUI: it fits body1 and body2 paragraphs, captions or form footers alike.

The interactive states are the browser’s native ones. data-disabled disables the link: on an <a> it sets aria-disabled="true", removes it from the tab order and blocks the click; on a <button> it uses disabled. Hover over it: the underline turns solid Press Tab: visible focus ring Disabled link

For an action that does not navigate but should look like a link inside text (“Resend code”, “Forgot your password?”), use <button data-mtx="link"> (MUI’s component="button"): no native background, border or padding, and it takes the surrounding typography. Without a type, the component sets type="button" so it does not submit forms. Didn't get the code? Resend code Resend in 30 s

To open in a new tab add target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer", and announce the change of context in the link text itself (or in its aria-label, which replaces the visible text for screen readers). MUI guide (opens in a new tab) Repository on GitHub
A sign-in form footer with secondary links, and breadcrumbs built with text links. Sign in Forgot your password? · Create an account Home / Projects / Materix UI
The styling is pure CSS: with hand-written classes no JavaScript is needed. data-mtx="link" is only required if you want the instance to be registered.

Declarative links initialize themselves. For dynamically created links: With ES modules: Attributes are read only when the instance is created: to change the color afterwards, change the class ( mtx-link--secondary, etc.) directly.

Always use an <a> with href: that way the link is focusable, activates with Enter and screen readers announce it as a link. For an action without a destination inside text use <button data-mtx="link">; for prominent actions, Button. The text must describe the destination (“Read the privacy policy”), not “click here”. Inside paragraphs keep the default underline ( always) so you don’t rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1, axe link-in-text-block); don’t use hover / none there. Keyboard focus shows a --mtx-focus-ring-width ring with a 2px offset. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves focus to the next or previous link. Enter Follows the link.

d: Temporary list of options anchored to a trigger: icons, dividers, selection, submenus, context menu and full keyboard navigation.

s.x: Menu displays a temporary list of actions or options on an elevated surface, anchored to the element that opens it, like MUI’s Menu (Popper + Paper + List). Use it for contextual actions on an item (edit, duplicate, delete), account menus or compact toolbars. To pick a value in a form use Select; for the app’s main navigation, use a Drawer or Tabs.

A trigger with data-open-menu="#id" and a data-mtx="menu" container with that id, holding data-mtx="menu-item" items. Clicking opens it below the trigger; clicking an option, clicking outside the menu, Escape or Tab closes it. Open menu Profile My account Log out When it opens, the menu container is moved to a portal at the end of <body> so it is not clipped by the overflow or z-index of its ancestors. It remains reachable with document.getElementById.

A menu needs an id and an explicit trigger; there is no implicit trigger. Three options, from most to least recommended: data-open-menu="#id" (or its alias data-mtx-menu-trigger="#id") on the button. It also works for triggers added after the menu is initialized (for example, the actions button of each row in a table rendered by JavaScript): clicks are handled through delegation. aria-controls="id" on an element that exists when the menu initializes. data-anchor="selector" on the menu itself: that element becomes both anchor and trigger. The component adds aria-haspopup="menu", a synchronized aria-expanded and aria-controls (when missing) to the trigger. Without any of these mechanisms the menu only opens programmatically with open(anchor). Annual report.pdf Budget.xlsx Rename Delete
data-icon inserts a Material Icons glyph before the item text. Edit Duplicate Share Delete

To separate groups use an <hr class="mtx-menu-item--divider"> or, with the simplified syntax, a <div data-mtx="menu-item" data-divider>: both are accessible separators ( role="separator"), leave an 8px vertical margin, and keyboard navigation skips them. File New Open… Save Print Close
data-dense on each item reduces its minimum height from 48px to 32px, for long menus on desktop. data-disable-gutters removes the horizontal padding. Format Single 1.15 1.5 Double

data-selected marks the current option with the action-selected background, and it receives focus when the menu is opened from the keyboard. data-disabled dims the option and excludes it from keyboard and click interaction ( aria-disabled="true"). Hover over the items to see the hover background. View: List List Grid Timeline (coming soon)

With role="menuitemcheckbox" the item toggles aria-checked when clicked; with role="menuitemradio" it becomes checked and unchecks the others in its group ( role="group" or the menu). data-checked sets the initial state and the component adds the mtx-menu-item__check mark, visible only while checked. mtx:menu:select includes detail.checked. View Ruler Gridlines Comfortable Compact

The menu is placed below the trigger, aligned to its left edge with a 4px gap. If it does not fit below and there is more room above, it opens upwards; its maximum height is the available space (with internal scrolling). While open it follows the trigger as the page scrolls, the window resizes or the trigger or menu change size, and it closes if the trigger leaves the viewport. Submenus open to the right of their item (to the left in RTL, dir="rtl"), flip to the other side when there is no room and shift vertically to stay inside the viewport. data-anchor="selector" uses another element as the anchor (and also turns it into a trigger). data-position-anchor="selector" only positions the menu against another element without turning it into a trigger (for example the whole ButtonGroup of a split button); focus still returns to the trigger. The menu’s previous sibling is no longer used as an implicit anchor: always declare the trigger (see “Triggers”). data-match-width makes the menu’s minimum width match the anchor’s. data-transform-origin forces the origin of the opening animation ( top, bottom …). The menu gets role="menu" and each item role="menuitem" (or the menuitemcheckbox / menuitemradio you declare, with a synchronized aria-checked) and tabindex="-1"; separators get role="separator". The trigger gets aria-haspopup="menu", aria-controls and a synchronized aria-expanded. When opened from the keyboard, focus moves to the selected option or the first enabled one; when opened with the mouse, to the menu container. When it closes with Escape or after a choice, focus returns to the trigger. Generated icons are decorative ( aria-hidden). If the trigger is an icon-only button, give it an aria-label. Disabled items carry aria-disabled="true" and are skipped by the keyboard. Key Action Enter / Space (on the trigger) Opens the menu and focuses the first option. ↓ / ↑ Next / previous option, wrapping around. Home / End First / last enabled option. Enter / Space Activates the focused option. Letter Jumps to the next option starting with that letter. → Opens the submenu of the focused item. ← Closes the submenu and returns to the parent menu. Escape Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Tab Closes the menu and lets focus move on.

d: Lets users pick a page within a large set of results, with ellipsis, first/last buttons and a link mode for SSR.

s.x: Pagination implements MUI’s Pagination: page buttons with ellipsis computed by the same algorithm as usePagination, previous/next buttons and optional first/last buttons, text and outlined variants, circular and rounded shapes, three sizes and three colors. Use it to move through result lists, blog articles or catalogs. For tables with “rows per page” and a range like “1–10 of 100”, use the Table TablePagination instead.
A single <nav data-mtx="pagination"> with data-count (total pages) and optionally data-page (1-based). The component generates the buttons, the ellipsis and the translated aria-label s.
data-variant="text" (default) or outlined.
data-shape="circular" (default) or rounded (4px radius).
data-size="small|medium|large": 26px, 32px (default) and 40px items, like MUI’s PaginationItem.
data-color="standard|primary|secondary" sets the color of the selected page.
Show the first and last page buttons with data-show-first-button and data-show-last-button; hide previous and next with data-hide-prev-button and data-hide-next-button.
data-sibling-count (1) sets how many pages are shown on each side of the current one, and data-boundary-count (1) how many at the beginning and the end.
Items have hover, focus-visible ( Tab) and ripple on press. Previous/next are disabled automatically at the ends; data-disabled disables the whole component.

With data-href-template every item is an <a href> ( {page} is replaced by the number): it works with server-side rendering, can open in a new tab and needs no JavaScript to navigate. Items that cannot navigate get aria-disabled="true" and no href. Progressive enhancement In link mode, clicking a page emits a cancelable mtx:pagination:change. If you call preventDefault(), the native navigation is cancelled and the component updates the current page in the client (useful to load the page with fetch and keep the links for crawlers and users without JavaScript).
Client-side paginated article list: mtx:pagination:change repaints the list.
Pre-rendered structure (SSR) that already looks right without JavaScript. If you add data-mtx="pagination", the component reuses the <ul> and repaints the items from data-count / data-page.

goTo(n), next() and previous() emit mtx:pagination:change; assigning page or count updates silently (useful to sync with external state without loops). previous() next() goTo(7) Page 1 With ES modules:

Landmark <nav> with aria-label="pagination navigation" (translated through i18n pagination.label; your own aria-label is kept). Give each pagination on the same page its own aria-label. Each page is a real <button> (or <a href> in link mode) with aria-label “Go to page N”; the current one has aria-current="page" and the label “page N”. Navigation buttons: “Go to first/previous/next/last page”; their SVG icon is aria-hidden. At the ends they are disabled with disabled (or aria-disabled in link mode). If the focused button becomes disabled after a change, focus moves to the current page. Focus is preserved on the same item after each repaint. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves through pages and navigation buttons. Enter / Space Activates the focused page or button ( Enter only in link mode).

d: Tabs to switch between views at the same level, with an animated indicator, icons, vertical orientation and full keyboard navigation.

s.x: Tabs organizes related content into views at the same level and lets users switch between them without leaving the page, with an indicator that slides under the active tab. Use it when there are between two and about seven sibling sections that users consult one at a time (profile, security, notifications). Don’t use it for sequential steps (use a wizard with buttons) or to navigate between top-level pages on mobile (use a Drawer).

A data-mtx="tabs" container with data-mtx="tab" buttons. Each tab points to its panel with data-panel="#id"; the component adds the ARIA roles and the indicator, hides inactive panels and activates the tab marked with data-active (or the first enabled one). Overview Activity Settings Project overview: 12 open tasks. Last activity 5 minutes ago. Project preferences. mtx-tabs-container is optional: it groups tabs and panels on an outlined surface. Without it, the tabs sit on the bottom divider line, as in MUI. Generated ids Tab ids are generated from the container’s id ( {id}-tab-1, {id}-tab-2 …). If the container has no id, a unique prefix per group is generated ( mtx-tabs-1, mtx-tabs-2 …), so several groups without an id never produce duplicate ids. Tabs and panels that already have an id keep it.

data-icon inserts a Material Icons glyph before the text. If the tab has no text, it becomes an icon-only tab: add an aria-label in that case. Recents Favorites Contacts The icon is always placed to the left of the text (equivalent to MUI’s iconPosition="start"); there is no top position.
data-full distributes the width among all tabs (equivalent to variant="fullWidth"), useful on mobile with few tabs. data-centered centers them. Inventory Sales Customers Yesterday Today Tomorrow

When the tabs don’t fit, the bar scrolls horizontally (touch, wheel or keyboard) and the indicator follows the active tab. The scrollbar is hidden and there are no arrow buttons, unlike MUI’s variant="scrollable". January February March April May June July August September October November December

data-orientation="vertical" stacks the tabs, places the indicator on the right and switches the navigation arrows to ↑ / ↓. Account Security Notifications Account details. Password and two-step verification. Email, push and weekly digest.

A tab with data-disabled (and disabled on the <button>) is shown dimmed, does not respond to clicks and is skipped by the keyboard. Hover to see the hover background and press Tab to see the focus ring. Active Disabled Available Colors The active tab and the indicator always use --mtx-color-primary; there are no attributes equivalent to MUI’s textColor or indicatorColor. For another color, redefine --mtx-color-primary on a container of the tabs.

By default the arrow keys only move focus and the tab is activated with Enter or Space (manual activation, the WAI-ARIA pattern recommended when loading a panel is expensive). With data-selection-follows-focus the tab is activated as soon as it receives focus (automatic activation, MUI’s default). Day Week Month Daily view. Weekly view. Monthly view.
Profile settings with full-width tabs, icons and panels with forms. Profile Security Alerts
With a hand-written structure the component reuses the existing indicator and honors mtx-tab--active as the initial tab.
With ES modules: General Advanced Blocked by event select('general') select('advanced')

Tabs ( data-mtx="tabs") Attribute Values Default Description data-orientation horizontal, vertical horizontal Orientation; also sets aria-orientation and the navigation arrow keys. data-full boolean — Distributes the width among the tabs ( mtx-tabs--full). data-centered boolean — Centers the tabs ( mtx-tabs--centered). data-selection-follows-focus boolean — Activates the tab when moving with the arrow keys (automatic activation). Tab ( data-mtx="tab") Attribute Values Default Description data-panel CSS selector — Panel controlled by the tab; it gets role="tabpanel" and is hidden when inactive. data-active boolean first enabled Initially active tab (the mtx-tab--active class also works). data-icon Material Icons name — Inserts a decorative icon before the text. data-value Text id or index Value returned by value and accepted by select(). data-disabled boolean — Disables the tab (adds aria-disabled). Combine it with disabled on the <button>. data-mtx="tab-panel" is registered as a generic component: it adds no behavior, and the mtx-tab-panel class is written by hand.

Class Description mtx-tabs Tab bar (flex, 48px, bottom divider line, horizontal scrolling without a visible scrollbar). mtx-tabs--full Equal-width tabs. mtx-tabs--centered Centered tabs. mtx-tabs--vertical Vertical orientation with the divider on the right. mtx-tabs__indicator 2px indicator (created if it does not exist). mtx-tabs-container Optional surface with border, radius and paper background for tabs + panels. mtx-tabs-container--borderless Container variant without border or background. mtx-tab Tab: 48px-high button, 90px minimum width, uppercase text. mtx-tab--active Active tab (primary color). mtx-tab__icon Icon generated by data-icon. mtx-tab-panel Content panel (16px × 24px padding; hidden with hidden).

Method Returns Description select(value) void Activates the tab by data-value, id, numeric index or element. Emits the events. value (getter) string | null data-value, id or index of the active tab. onBeforeChange (property) — Function (tab, panel, previousTab, previousPanel); if it returns false, the change is canceled. onChange (property) — Function (tab, panel, previousTab, previousPanel) called after the change. destroy() void Removes the listeners and the ResizeObserver. Unlinks the instance: getInstance() then returns undefined.

Event detail Fired when mtx:tabs:before-change { tab, panel, previousTab, previousPanel } Before switching tabs. Cancelable with preventDefault(). mtx:tabs:change { tab, panel, previousTab, previousPanel } After another tab is activated (click, keyboard or select()). Not fired on the initial activation.

Variable Usage --mtx-color-primary Active tab text and indicator. --mtx-color-text-secondary, --mtx-color-text-primary Text at rest and on hover. --mtx-color-action-hover Hover background. --mtx-color-action-disabled Disabled text. --mtx-color-divider Divider line and container border. --mtx-color-background-paper, --mtx-shape-radius Background and radius of mtx-tabs-container. --mtx-focus-ring-width, --mtx-focus-ring-color Focus ring. --mtx-duration-standard, --mtx-duration-shorter, --mtx-easing-standard Indicator and color animation. --mtx-spacing-1, --mtx-font-family Icon-text gap and typography.

The container gets role="tablist" and aria-orientation; each tab role="tab", aria-selected and aria-controls; each panel role="tabpanel" and aria-labelledby. Ids are generated if missing. Only the active tab is in the tab order ( tabindex="0"); the others use tabindex="-1" and are reached with the arrow keys ( roving tabindex). Disabled tabs carry aria-disabled="true" and are skipped by the keyboard. Icon-only tabs need an aria-label; the generated icon is decorative ( aria-hidden). Key Action Tab Enters the active tab; the next Tab leaves the bar. → / ← Next / previous tab (horizontal), wrapping around. ↓ / ↑ Next / previous tab (vertical), wrapping around. Home / End First / last enabled tab. Enter / Space Activates the focused tab (manual activation).

d: Floating action button that reveals three to six related, labeled actions in four directions, on click or on hover.

s.x: SpeedDial is a primary Fab that, when pressed, reveals several secondary actions as small labeled FABs, just like MUI’s SpeedDial. Use it when a screen’s primary action has three to six related variants (create document, spreadsheet, presentation). If there is only one action, use a Fab; if there are many options or they are not creation actions, use a Menu.

A data-mtx="speed-dial" container with data-icon (the primary FAB icon) and data-label (its accessible name), and inside it one <button> per action with data-icon and data-tooltip. The component builds the primary FAB, the actions container and the labels. Accessible name for each action data-tooltip creates the visible label and, if the button has no aria-label / aria-labelledby, is also copied to aria-label, so icon-only actions always have an accessible name. When closed, the actions are invisible but still take up their space in the layout flow, as in MUI: place the SpeedDial in a corner with absolute or fixed positioning (see the “Position” section).
data-direction sets where the actions open: up (default), down, left or right. Vertically, labels appear to the left of each action; horizontally, above it.
data-color on the container colors the primary FAB ( primary by default), and on each action, that action’s FAB ( secondary by default). It accepts the palette colors.

By default the labels of all actions are visible while the SpeedDial is open (equivalent to MUI’s tooltipOpen), styled like the Tooltip. With data-tooltip-hover each action uses a real Tooltip ( data-mtx-tooltip) that appears on hover or keyboard focus, to the left for vertical directions and above for horizontal ones; recommended for horizontal directions so they don’t overlap. Keyboard In both modes the label is visible while tabbing through the actions: in the persistent mode it always is, and with data-tooltip-hover the Tooltip appears on keyboard focus and hides with Escape. Each action’s accessible name is still its aria-label (persistent labels are aria-hidden so they are not read twice).
data-event="hover" opens the SpeedDial when the pointer enters and closes it when it leaves. Clicking the FAB still toggles it, so it also works on touch screens and with the keyboard.

The mtx-speed-dial--fixed-br and mtx-speed-dial--fixed-bl classes pin it 24px from the bottom-right or bottom-left corner of the viewport, above the content ( z-index 1050). There is no declarative “always open” mode: to show it expanded, call open() (see “Programmatic usage”).
Actions for a photo gallery: each action performs its task and closes the SpeedDial. Choose an action.
With a hand-written structure the component reuses the FAB and the actions container, and only wraps each action that has data-tooltip in mtx-speed-dial__action-wrapper.
With ES modules: open() close() direction = right / up

SpeedDial ( data-mtx="speed-dial") Attribute Values Default Description data-icon Material Icons name — Generates the primary FAB if neither.mtx-speed-dial__fab nor.mtx-fab exists. The icon rotates 45° when open. data-label Text i18n speedDial.actions ( Actions / Acciones) aria-label of the generated primary FAB. data-color primary, secondary, error, warning, info, success primary Color of the generated primary FAB. data-direction up, down, left, right up Opening direction. data-event click, hover click With hover it also opens when the pointer enters and closes when it leaves. data-tooltip-hover boolean — Replaces the persistent labels with one Tooltip per action (hover and keyboard focus). Action (child <button>, simplified syntax) Attribute Values Default Description data-icon Material Icons name — Action icon. data-tooltip Text — Visible label next to the action; also its aria-label when it has none. data-color Palette colors secondary Color of the action’s small FAB. aria-label Text — Accessible name (required; not generated).

Class Description mtx-speed-dial Flex container ( z-index 1050). mtx-speed-dial--direction-up / --down / --left / --right Opening direction. mtx-speed-dial--open Open state: actions visible and primary icon rotated 45°. mtx-speed-dial--tooltip-hover Tooltip label mode (hover/focus). mtx-speed-dial--fixed-br / mtx-speed-dial--fixed-bl Pinned 24px from the bottom-right / bottom-left corner. mtx-speed-dial__fab Primary FAB. mtx-speed-dial__actions Actions container (12px gap). mtx-speed-dial__action Small FAB for each action. mtx-speed-dial__action-wrapper Action + label wrapper, with a staggered animation. mtx-speed-dial__tooltip Persistent action label (default mode, aria-hidden).

Method Returns Description open() void Reveals the actions and sets aria-expanded="true" on the FAB. close() void Collapses the actions. toggle() void Toggles the state. isOpen (getter) boolean Open state. direction (get/set) string Current direction; setting it changes the class. destroy() void Removes the listeners from the FAB, the container and the document.

Event detail Fired when mtx:speed-dial:open { speedDial } It opens (click, hover or open()). mtx:speed-dial:close { speedDial } It closes (click, click away, Escape, pointer leaving or close()). The previous names mtx-speed-dial-open and mtx-speed-dial-close are still emitted as deprecated aliases until 1.0.

Variable Usage --mtx-duration-short, --mtx-duration-shorter, --mtx-easing-standard Icon rotation, appearance of actions and labels. --mtx-tooltip-bg, --mtx-tooltip-color, --mtx-tooltip-font-size, --mtx-tooltip-max-width Persistent labels (the same tokens as the Tooltip). --mtx-font-family Label typography. The primary FAB and the actions use the Fab variables.

The primary FAB gets aria-haspopup="true" and a synchronized aria-expanded; its name comes from data-label (or from the aria-label you write in the BEM syntax). Actions are native <button> elements with a decorative icon ( aria-hidden): they need an aria-label. While the SpeedDial is closed, the actions container gets inert and aria-hidden="true" and each action tabindex="-1", so invisible actions are out of the tab order; opening restores them. The FAB has aria-controls pointing to the actions container. Persistent labels have aria-hidden="true" (the name is already in the aria-label); with data-tooltip-hover the Tooltip does not duplicate the name when it matches the text. It respects prefers-reduced-motion through the global CssBaseline rule. Key Action Enter / Space on the FAB Opens or closes the SpeedDial. Tab / Shift + Tab Moves through the actions. Enter / Space on an action Runs the action. Escape Closes the SpeedDial and returns focus to the FAB (and hides the visible Tooltip).

d: Shows progress through a sequence of numbered steps, horizontal or vertical, linear or with clickable steps, plus its compact mobile version.

s.x: Stepper conveys progress through a process split into steps (sign-up, checkout, setup wizard): which step is active, which are completed and which are still ahead. Use it when order matters and each step makes sense on its own. Don’t use it to switch between views at the same level (use Tabs) or to show the progress of an ongoing operation (use Progress).

An <ol data-mtx="stepper"> with one <li data-label> per step. The component generates the 24px numbered icon, the connectors and the accessible text (“Step 2 of 3”), and marks the active step with aria-current="step". data-active-step is the zero-based index of the active step.

In linear mode (the default), steps before the active one are considered completed and the following ones disabled. Buttons with data-mtx-stepper-action="back|next|reset" and data-target="#id" drive the stepper without writing JavaScript; data-panel on each step shows its panel only while it is active, and data-finished-panel shows the final panel once activeStep reaches the number of steps. Step 1: choose the goal and the budget. Step 2: define audiences and placements. Step 3: write the ad. All steps completed. Back Next Reset back buttons are disabled automatically on the first step and next buttons once finished (add data-keep-enabled to opt out).
data-alternative-label places the label below the icon and splits the width evenly. It is the most robust option on narrow screens.

With data-non-linear every step is a <button> (StepButton) with ripple, visible focus and activation with Enter or Space, and users can jump to any step. Completion is no longer inferred from the order: set it with data-completed or setCompleted().

data-orientation="vertical" stacks the steps. The <li> content becomes StepContent, which expands with a transition only on the active step (or always, with data-expanded). Inside the stepper, data-mtx-stepper-action without data-target acts on its own stepper. Choose the campaign type, the country and the daily budget. Continue An ad group contains one or more ads that share the same audience. Continue Back Write the headline and check the preview. Finish Back
By default the StepIcon is the step number. data-icon uses a custom Material Icon (24px, no forced size). A completed step shows a check and a step with an error shows a warning, replacing the icon.

Active, completed, optional ( data-optional, with custom text when given a value), error with message ( data-error="message") and disabled ( data-disabled). The connector before an active or completed step takes the primary color. Responsive behavior Below 600px, a horizontal stepper without alternative label only shows the label of the active step; the others are visually hidden but still available to screen readers. If every label must be visible on mobile, use data-alternative-label or the vertical orientation.

data-mtx="mobile-stepper" is MUI’s compact version: it generates the Back/Next buttons and a dots (default), text (“2 / 5”) or progress indicator (reusing LinearProgress). data-position="bottom|top" pins it to the edge of the window.

Account sign-up with validation: the cancelable mtx:stepper:change event prevents moving forward when the email is invalid and flags the step with an error. Team plan · $12 per user per month. Back Next

For SSR or fine-grained control: if each <li class="mtx-step"> already contains.mtx-step__label-container, the component reuses it (no duplicated connectors or labels) and only paints the icon, the accessible text and the states.
With ES modules: back() next() setCompleted(active) setError(active) reset()

Stepper ( data-mtx="stepper", on an <ol>) Attribute Values Default Description data-active-step number (0 … steps) 0 Index of the active step. Equal to the number of steps = finished. Updated while navigating. data-orientation horizontal, vertical horizontal Orientation. In vertical, the <li> content is a collapsible StepContent. data-alternative-label boolean — Label below the icon (horizontal only). data-non-linear boolean — Clickable steps ( <button>); completion is not inferred from the order. data-finished-panel CSS selector — Element shown only when finished ( activeStep === length). data-label text — aria-label of the <ol> when it has none. Step (child <li>) Attribute Values Default Description data-label text <li> text Step label. Without data-label, a text-only <li> uses that text. data-optional boolean or text — Shows the translated “Optional” caption or the given text. data-completed boolean, "false" from the order (linear) Forces the completed state (or prevents it with "false"). data-error text or empty — Error state with a warning icon; the text is shown as the message. data-disabled boolean — Step cannot be activated ( <button disabled> in non-linear). data-icon Mate

Class Description mtx-stepper Root (flex, no list styles). mtx-stepper--horizontal, mtx-stepper--vertical Orientation. mtx-stepper--alternative-label Label below the icon, equal-width steps. mtx-stepper--non-linear Non-linear mode. mtx-stepper--finished All steps passed. mtx-step Step ( <li>). mtx-step--active, mtx-step--completed, mtx-step--error, mtx-step--disabled, mtx-step--expanded, mtx-step--last Step states. mtx-step__label-container StepLabel ( <span>, or <button> in non-linear). mtx-step-button StepButton (non-linear): ripple, hover and focus. mtx-step__icon-container, mtx-step-icon Container and 24px StepIcon. mtx-step-icon--number, --completed, --error, --custom, --active Icon variants. mtx-step__label-text, mtx-step__label, mtx-step__optional Texts: label and caption (optional or error message). mtx-step__sr Screen-reader-only text. mtx-step-connector, mtx-step-connector__line StepConnector. mtx-step__content, mtx-step__content-inner Collapsible StepContent (vertical). mtx-mobile-stepper, mtx-mobile-stepper--{dots,text,progress}, --{static,bottom,top} MobileStepper and its variants. mtx-mobile-stepper__back, __next, __indicator, __dot, __dot--active, __progress, __statu

Stepper Method Returns Description next() boolean Moves to the next enabled step (up to “finished”). back() boolean Moves to the previous enabled step. goTo(index) boolean Activates the index (0 … length). false when out of range, disabled or canceled. reset() boolean Returns to step 0 and clears completed and error states. setCompleted(index, completed = true) this Marks or unmarks a step as completed. setError(index, message) this Text = error with message; true = error without message; false = clears. setDisabled(index, disabled = true) this Enables or disables a step. isCompleted(index) boolean Effective completed state of the step. refresh() void Re-reads the <li> elements after adding or removing steps. activeStep (getter/setter) number Active step; assigning it is the same as goTo(). length, finished (getters) number, boolean Number of steps and whether all were passed. destroy() void Removes the listeners. Unlinks the instance: getInstance() then returns undefined. MobileStepper: next(), back(), goTo(index), reset(), setSteps(count), activeStep, steps, destroy().

Event detail Fired when mtx:stepper:change { activeStep, previousStep } ( reset: true from reset()) Before the step changes (click, trigger or API). Cancelable with preventDefault() for validation. Fired by both Stepper and MobileStepper.

Variable Usage --mtx-stepper-connector-color Connector and StepContent border color (grey 400 in light, grey 600 in dark). --mtx-stepper-icon-size StepIcon size (24px). --mtx-color-primary, --mtx-color-primary-contrast Active/completed icon, active connector and number. --mtx-color-text-disabled Icon of pending steps. --mtx-color-text-primary, --mtx-color-text-secondary Labels. --mtx-color-error Step with error. --mtx-color-action-hover, --mtx-focus-ring-* StepButton hover and focus. --mtx-color-background-default, --mtx-color-action-disabled, --mtx-z-index-mobile-stepper MobileStepper.

A semantic <ol> is used: the order of the steps is part of the meaning. Name it with aria-label. The active step carries aria-current="step" (on the <li>, or on its <button> in non-linear mode). Each step includes hidden text with its position and state: “Step 2 of 3: Shipping, completed”. Icons and connectors are decorative ( aria-hidden). Texts are translated from the document lang or data-locale. In non-linear mode steps are native <button> elements with visible focus; disabled ones use disabled. In vertical, the content of collapsed steps is marked inert and aria-hidden so it cannot receive focus. MobileStepper announces the current step in an aria-live="polite" region; dots and the bar are decorative. Honors prefers-reduced-motion. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves through clickable steps (non-linear) and the Back/Next buttons. Enter / Space Activates the focused step or button.

d: SemVer versioning, changelog, the package contents and the exact steps to release Materix UI to npm with prepublishOnly checks and Git tags.

s.x: Materix UI follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer) with the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. MAJOR: changes that are incompatible with the public API (breaking changes). MINOR: new backward-compatible features. PATCH: backward-compatible bug fixes. The public API is everything a consumer can rely on: data-mtx names and data-* attributes, BEM classes, design tokens ( --mtx-*), the JavaScript API ( Materix.*, component methods), the mtx:* event names and their detail, the exports paths of the package and the TypeScript types.

Before 1.0.0, a MINOR release may contain breaking changes. Each one is listed in CHANGELOG.md and explained in MIGRATION.md (how to detect it and how to migrate, with before/after snippets). Renamed events keep emitting the old name as a deprecated alias until 1.0.0. A component is not considered stable until it has an implementation, a working example, bilingual documentation and tests.
Semantic prefixes make it easy to write the changelog:

package.json publishes only dist/, types/, README.md, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md and MIGRATION.md (field files). Examples, documentation, templates and tests are not published. Field Value main dist/materix.umd.cjs (CommonJS) module dist/materix.es.js types types/index.d.ts style dist/materix.min.css unpkg / jsdelivr dist/materix.umd.js (the default file of https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@rubenchodev/materix-ui) exports.,./core,./components/*,./components/*.css,./base.css,./utilities.css,./materix.min.css,./dist/* sideEffects CSS files and dist/**/*.js (the modules register components when imported) npm run build runs three steps: the full bundle ( vite build), the per-component modules ( vite build -c vite.modules.config.js) and the TypeScript declarations ( node scripts/gen-types.mjs, which writes types/lib and types/components from the JSDoc in src/). The files written by hand, types/index.d.ts, types/core.d.ts and types/events.d.ts, refine that base; npm run types:check compiles tests/types/*.ts against them.

The package is published from the root of the materix-ui repository. Update the changelog. Move the entries of ## [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md to a new ## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD section (Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed). If there are breaking changes, update MIGRATION.md. Bump the version in package.json and in docs/hugo.toml ( params.version, shown in the docs and used by the playground CDN links). Use npm version without a tag, so the commit and tag are created only after a successful publish (step 5): Check the package contents (it runs no scripts): The list must contain only dist/, types/, the README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG and MIGRATION files. Log in and publish. prepublishOnly runs npm run build, npm test and npm run types:check; if any of them fails, nothing is published. publishConfig.access is public. To try the release from a real install first, use npm pack and install the generated.tgz in a test project. Commit and tag the release: Publish a GitHub release from the tag with the changelog notes, and redeploy the documentation.
Publish betas under a dist-tag so npm install @rubenchodev/materix-ui keeps installing the stable version:
npm does not allow republishing a version. Publish a new PATCH with the fix and, if needed, deprecate the faulty one:

d: Materix UI development status: completed milestones and pending work.

s.x: Define the name and naming convention. Define the vanilla CSS + JS architecture. Define the mtx- prefix. Define declarative initialization. Create the project’s base structure. Configure Vite. Create the initial Button + Ripple component. Adapt the design tokens to the MUI look and feel. Implement the Light theme. Implement the Dark theme. Reset: keep only the Button component. Build TextField with the MUI variations (outlined/filled/standard, small, margins, multiline, select, adornments, hidden label, colors). Build additional components following MUI (List, Tabs, etc.). Build Paper, Divider and IconButton following MUI. Build Card, Checkbox, Switch, Dialog and Select (extended native select with search and multiple selection) following MUI. Rewrite Select and create Chip, NativeSelect, Radio, Menu, MenuItem, List, Typography, Link, Avatar, Badge, Alert, Snackbar, Tabs, Drawer and Table following MUI. Create /examples/button. Complete the Hugo documentation for Button. Address Button accessibility. Define the SemVer versioning strategy. Define the npm publishing strategy. Evaluate an optional MutationObserver for dynamic content. Create automated tests for critical components.
